#1974. Michael Carrick ‘pretty clear’ on Man Utd future despite relegation woes

Michael Carrick remains confident in his ability to oversee Manchester United’s resurgence after a “right mixed” three weeks left his team in the relegation zone and the head coach’s future under scrutiny.

The 20-time league champions will spend the November international break in 18th place as their wait to add to August’s solitary Premier League win against Ipswich continued against Aston Villa.

United showed spirit and all too familiar flaws as Sunday’s helter-skelter clash ended in a 4-4 draw after substitutes Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu scored in stoppage time following Tuesday’s 3-2 comeback win against Roma.

Carrick insisted afterwards that he would not walk away from a job that looked like it could be taken from him a fortnight ago and the international break provides an opportunity for the club to take stock.

Asked if the two-week pause comes at a good time for the group, the under-fire United boss said: “Yeah, it’s been a right mixed week or two or three, really, if you’re looking at the events.

“But I’m pretty clear where we need to go and how we need to get there.

“Obviously some of the boys will be flying off around the world and different things, and the group will be split for 10 days or so.

“But as a normal international week is, you know, we’ll have some training. We’ll have one or two days off, but not too much. But we’ll train, and we’ll get ready for the next game.”

The final international break of the year would be a logical time for United to make a change given there is no free midweek until mid-December after returning with a trip to rivals Liverpool on November 22.

The Open to return to historic Scottish venue after 11 years

Hearts set for six-man injury boost as Wouter Vrancken bullish over revival

Hearts crisis or just a bad week, is Vrancken in trouble and has Jamestown failed?

But Carrick is steadfast in his belief that he can lead the embattled side up the standings having seen enough positives since a 4-1 defeat at Como and 3-0 home loss to Bournemouth left his job hanging by a thread.

United failed to take their chances and saw Lisandro Martinez sent off in a 2-0 loss at Chelsea, before Tuesday’s stirring 3-2 Champions League comeback against Roma was followed by the dramatic Villa draw.

“Goals change games, and you’ve got to deal with it, and it’s part of something we have to improve on drastically,” Carrick said.

“But there’s more than enough. We’re just making it too difficult for ourselves at the moment in certain times.”

Carrick is far from perfect but has been let down by United’s transfer business in the view of outspoken defender Martinez and the fans who frequently aim chants at director of football Jason Wilcox.

Left-back was among the areas of need and Luke Shaw’s injury has seen Diogo Dalot often deployed there, but frustrations with the United full-back reached boiling point on Sunday as supporters cheered his substitution.

Head coach Carrick, who was unaware of United’s full-back then being hounded as he left the ground, said: “We’ve got to be careful with that, I think.

“I understand the frustration. I understand the disappointment of the supporters, so I get it. We’re all frustrated. We’re all disappointed.

“The players are as much as anyone, I guarantee you that. Diogo gives absolutely everything. He’s played in different positions. He’s played left-back. He’s played really well at times.

“He gives a penalty away. He knows that, maybe he can do a little bit better. Alright, that’s part of it, he’s made a mistake.

“But he cares an awful lot, and he’s given everything, so I like what he brings to the team. I like what he brings to the group.”

#1973. Three Bridges show spirit to earn point against Brentwood

Bridges were desperate to get points on the board, but perhaps even more importantly, to rediscover the battling spirit that had been missing during last week's disappointing performance away at Maldon & Tiptree.

Jamie Crellin's men responded positively, showing plenty of fight and determination.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

After an even opening, the hosts took the lead in the 12th minute through October's player of the month, Ade Adeyinka. David Przybylo played him through the middle and, from around 20 yards out, he unleashed an unstoppable strike into the net to give Bridges an early advantage.

The remainder of the first half was evenly matched, with Roberts producing several good saves in the Bridges goal. At the other end, the energetic Villavicencio continued to cause problems for the visitors, particularly with a dangerous cross towards Reece Hallard, whose header from six yards narrowly missed the target.

It could have been 2-0 moments into the second half as, straight from the restart, Bridges put together an excellent move down the right. Velvick released Przybylo through on goal, but under pressure from the goalkeeper, his effort narrowly drifted wide.

Brentwood began to pile on the pressure at the other end and found their reward in the 58th minute. Following a free-kick from Reid, Gibbs slotted his effort into the bottom corner to restore parity.

Just a couple of minutes later, Przybylo, who had been a constant handful for the visitors, worked his way past his marker and had another opportunity to restore Bridges' advantage, but his effort narrowly missed the far post.

With Bridges short of options on the bench and several players playing through injuries, maintaining the intensity became increasingly difficult. Brentwood Town took control during the final 20 minutes, but Roberts came to the rescue with two superb saves to deny Cerulli and Sears, while the Bridges players continued to put their bodies on the line to protect their point.

There was late drama in the 94th minute when Reece Hallard chased a ball through on the counter-attack, only for Cripps to handle it as the last man.

The Brentwood defender was shown a straight red card, leaving the visitors down to ten men. However, it came too late to have any impact on the outcome, as the match finished 1-1.

The point represents a much-needed response from Bridges, who are now into a demanding run of three consecutive away fixtures in seven days against Cray Wanderers (Tuesday 10), Welling United (Saturday 14) and Dartford (Tuesday 17).

#1972. Scotland international celebrates Pocognoli call-up with rare assist but is left to rue 52 second mistake

Scotland international Ryan Porteous celebrated his recall to the national team by grabbing a rare assist for LAFC, but was left to rue an early mistake as his side fell to a 2-1 away defeat against Seattle Sounders on Sunday night.

Porteous, 27, was named in the Scotland squad by head coach Sebastien Pocognoli as an injury replacement for Stephen Welsh at the weekend, with the Swansea City defender ruled out after picking up an injury in the 3-1 EFL Championship defeat to Portsmouth last Tuesday.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It means Porteous could make his first Scotland appearance since he was introduced as a late substitute in the 1-0 Nations League play-off win in Greece back in March 2025, as the national team prepares for a double-header against North Macedonia and Switzerland later this week.

The former Hibs centre-back added to his successful week by picking up his first assist of the season for Los Angeles FC as they fell to a narrow defeat at Seattle in their last regular season game. However, the clash began in disastrous fashion for the visitors, with Slovakian international Albert Rusnak putting Seattle into the lead after just 52 seconds at Lumen Field.

With Los Angeles in possession of the ball from kick-off, Hugo Lloris’ attempt to pass the ball back to Porteous caused confusion, with the Scottish defender and Mathieu Choiniere appearing to get in each other’s way. The latter lost the ball under pressure, allowing Cristian Roldan to pinch the ball and cross for Rusnak to tap into an empty net to put the home side into an early lead.

The home side then added a second just after the half-hour mark through winger Sebastian Gomez, with the 20-year-old’s shot from just inside the area deflecting into the top corner beyond Lloris to put the hosts into a commanding first-half lead as they looked to get a win that would seal their place in the end-of-season MLS playoffs, which begins later this month.

LAFC did their best to launch a comeback, with the visitors having 13 attempts on goal in the second 45 to Seattle’s zero. However, they couldn’t to find a breakthrough until the 82nd minute, with Porteous rising highest to Leo Walta’s free-kick, and heading across goal for centre-back partner Eddie Segura to bullet home and reduce the deficit.

In the end, though, the second-half onslaught was not enough to rescue a point in the Emerald City, as LAFC ended the regular Western Conference season in sixth place on 47 points, with 12 wins, 11 draws and 11 defeats, setting up a round of 16 clash with St. Louis City in the MLS playoffs on November 23.

“Conceding a goal inside the first minute completely changes the game plan,” lamented LAFC defender Segura. “We can't keep putting ourselves in a position where we are chasing matches from the opening whistle. It is a bad habit we have to fix immediately before the playoffs start.”

#1970. Ref watch: Dermot Gallagher makes telling Brentford and Igor Thiago observation after red card at Brighton

Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher believes Igor Thiago's red card in the 2-0 loss at Brighton was ”not a terrible decision.”

Brentford striker Thiago was initially shown a yellow card by referee Michael Oliver after reacting to a shirt pull and subsequent push from Albion midfielder Chema Andres, who was also booked.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

But the punishment was upgraded to red on review as match official Oliver deemed the Brazil international used “force” to push his opponent in the face with a raised arm.

Brentford were already trailing at the time of Thiago’s sending-off following a stunning long-range opener from Brighton midfielder Diego Gomez.

Pascal Gross doubled Albion’s lead with a 42nd-minute penalty awarded for Keane Lewis-Potter’s shirt pull on Luka Vuskovic.

Gallagher, speaking on Sky Sports Ref Watch, said: "I'll be saying to players, this is what referees are doing.

“This is how they're acting, why put yourself in this position? We've had three [incidents like this] over the last few weeks.

“I said, don't give the referee a decision today.”

Fellow Ref Watch pundit Jay Bothroyd then chipped in: “I'm sorry, first of all, the [Brighton] defender [Chema] has initiated that whole incident, right? He's caused that incident.

“When I look at that, to me, Thiago's just trying to strike him off. His arm has brushed up his shirt and hit him in the face.

“You can't give red cards for that. I'm sorry. You just can't. That is a terrible decision to make.”

Gallagher though backed Oliver as he was working within the rules. He responded: “It's a wrong decision. I'll accept that, a wrong decision.

“Not a terrible decision, because the referees have asked. I get that you think it's wrong, but it's not a terrible decision.”

Meanwhile, Brentford boss Keith Andrews questioned the use of VAR in the Premier League after the Thiago incident.

“I’m struggling to believe in this day and age where we see the referee’s call on pitch and the bar of where they’re given the licence to referee in-game, which is what I should think it should be, but he’s been sent to the screen,” he said.

“We play on the edge, we’re a team that likes to play on the edge, I want us to be on the edge. But it clearly cost us.”

In several cases, it’s fair to say that the players aren’t up to the task. Filippo Terracciano’s role is emblematic: already rejected by the previous management, he remained with Milan at Amorim’s request.

Pervis Estupinan, on the other hand, seems to have completely disappeared from the radar, having remained on the bench for the entire match against Ferencvaros. The two left-backs have a lot of work to do, and this could influence some transfer choices too.

#1967. I witnessed recurring Celtic Remembrance Sunday embarrassment but Green Brigade act commended

Despite some rocky results, Celtic have made it to another international break still in front of Rangers. They are four points clear of the second-placed Ibrox side, who have a game in hand, after a narrow 1-0 Remembrance Sunday win over Kilmarnock.

Parkhead is unlike most places in the United Kingdom on Remembrance Sunday. Before kick-off, as fans milled around outside the stadium, there was barely a single poppy visible.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

This was the 13th time since 1974, when Celtic first played a Sunday fixture, that they have been in action on Remembrance Sunday itself, the fifth time at home.

People wondered beforehand what would happen and whether a period of silence would be attempted at all. After all, when Celtic published their Kilmarnock matchday guide, including “everything you need to know about the game”, there was no mention of the day’s significance. All it advised was that supporters should be in their seat for the 4pm kick-off – put back due to Remembrance Sunday activities in Glasgow - to “make some noise for the Bhoys”. Well, many certainly managed this.

The Tannoy announcer stated there would be “some moments” of silence to commemorate the war dead. The Green Brigade opted to stay outside, which is to be commended. They clearly took the view that if others wished to take part in the tribute, then they could.

However, so many elsewhere in the stadium reacted by booing and jeering once John Beaton had blown his whistle to signal the start of the tribute that the referee swiftly ended. The ‘tribute’ was timed at just 13 seconds, which is some way short of the minute that is the norm on such occasions.

To be fair, the announcer had said the plan was for a "few moments’ silence" rather than a full minute. But there was barely even a few moments’ worth.

One wonders if Beaton had been given a recommendation by the authorities to wrap things up as quickly as possible if the booing started, because he did so almost immediately. Although it was an ugly cacophony, maybe it might have been better if he had just stood his ground and let it play out.

Others might argue it would have been better if the silence had not been scheduled – or attempted – at all. Everyone knew what was going to happen.

But then what about the Celtic fans who do wish to pay their respects – and there were plenty. And the Kilmarnock fans, small group though they were, had every right to expect to be able to stand and remember relatives who had made the greatest sacrifice.

The Green Brigade stayed away, which was fair enough. But many inside the ground, according to testimonies on Facebook and elsewhere, explained that they had wanted to observe a silence. The Celtic board have enough on their plate without seeking more aggravation. They are probably just happy that it's all over for another year. However, the vexed question of war remembrance is a recurring issue that embarrasses the club annually.

The issue of Kasper Hogh’s Parkhead goal drought dominated the post-match debate as did Mika Baur’s worrying ankle injury. So focus was not necessarily on the Parkhead return of Luke McCowan, whom many once wondered if they might ever see in a Celtic shirt again.

He was sent on in the dying minutes against Falkirk last weekend when Celtic were in dire straits. The stakes were higher this time. He replaced Benjamin Nygren with eight minutes left, and with Celtic desperate to hold on to a 1-0 lead. It was his first home appearance for Celtic since being taken off at half-time against Rangers on 20 September. You just can’t keep a good (Celtic) man down.

Some questioned whether he could ever recover from his disastrous cameo appearance against LASK in August as Celtic tumbled out of Champions League qualifying at the hands of their Austrian opponents.

After a few weeks in purdah, he started the league clash against Rangers just before the last international break. It didn’t go well. The midfielder was replaced at half time with Celtic trailing 1-0.

Might this stand as McCowan’s last appearance? Again, many assumed so. Tony Docherty, his former Dundee manager and now in charge of the Scotland Under-21s, recently mentioned on a podcast that the player was “having a tough time” having been bombed out of the squad completely.

However, the boyhood Celtic fan isn’t giving up on his Celtic career, that’s clear. Just as Hogh received warm applause when he left the field after 70 minutes, McCowan was greeted with similar when he was announced as coming on.

Admittedly, you feared for him slightly. Celtic were still hanging on to a 1-0 lead and it was getting increasingly nervy. One misplaced pass could have had dire consequence. But he was tidy and busy, and he even saw an effort slip through Nico Mantl’s fingers and into the net, although the whistle had already blown for a foul. Fans cheered, possibly slightly cruelly.

Who knows what it means for his Celtic future? Martin O’Neill didn’t broach the subject of McCowan specifically afterwards but he was asked about an unusual looking squad, which featured just one- goalkeeper Sam Johnstone - of the six late summer transfer deadline day acquisitions. Haissem Hassan, meanwhile, was a glaring omission. On this subject, O’Neill explained, slightly mysteriously, that it was all to do with squad “manoeuvring”.

By Lewis Nolan | 07 Nov 2026 15:20

Tottenham Hotspur's loss to Leeds United means they have failed to win any of the past 39 matches in the Premier League in which they conceded first (D9, L30), an unwanted record in the competition.

Spurs were hopeful of securing a fourth consecutive win in the Premier League, but they instead suffered a 1-0 defeat at Elland Road, with Noah Okafor scoring a late winner.

The result leaves the Londoners in 10th place with 12 points after 10 matchweeks, but they are only three points from 16th-placed Coventry City.

Roberto De Zerbi will be particularly concerned by his team's failure to find the back of the net after going behind, with the club having only scored 10 times in the top flight so far.

Opta data shows that Spurs have in fact failed to win any of their last 39 Premier League games in which they conceded first, their longest ever run in the competition.

39 - Tottenham Hotspur have failed to win any of their last 39 games in the Premier League in which they've conceded the opening goal (D9 L30); their longest ever run in the competition. Setback. https://t.co/0FfwlLIXO1

Though Leeds could have been reduced to 10 men in the first half, a possible VAR error should not distract from the fact that Spurs looked poor offensively yet again.

The Londoners produced seven shots to the victors' 16 on Saturday, and no player in the visiting team produced more than one shot on target.

Despite signing the likes of Omar Marmoush and Savio in the summer transfer window, De Zerbi's side have rarely offered any threat in the final third.

James Maddison's creativity has been missed, but his absence cannot explain why they have failed to score in half of their Premier League games this season.

Spurs have finished 17th in the Premier League in each of the last two seasons, so nobody at the club can afford to take safety for granted.

Tottenham could end the weekend in 14th place, and the gap to the bottom three could be as small as two points.

De Zerbi has not been able to eradicate all of the defensive mistakes that have plagued the Londoners, and given his players have frequently struggled in the final third, it would not be surprising if they battled against demotion yet again.

#1962. Scotland given major boost as key midfielder extends 120-day exile ahead of Nations League fixture

Scotland have been handed a major boost as they prepare to return to Nations League action after it was confirmed that Switzerland captain Granit Xhaka has withdrawn from the squad ahead of the team’s clash in St Gillen next week.

Xhaka, 34, has been forced to pull out of the Switzerland squad after picking up a calf injury in Sunderland’s 1-0 win over Chelsea in the English Premier League on Sunday, with the Swiss FA confirming he will play no part in their upcoming fixtures against Slovenia and Scotland this month.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Forced off just three minutes into the Stadium of Light clash, Sunderland head coach Regis Le Bris confirmed he had been struggling with a problem before the game, his 50th for the Black Cats. “It looks like a calf injury,” said the Frenchman. “But we don't know exactly the timeframe at the minute. It was just the last sprint of the warm-up; that's often the case [with these injuries].

The news means that Xhaka, capped an astonishing 152 times by his country, has now been absent from international duty for the last 120 days. He also withdrew from last month’s reverse fixture at Hampden Park amid a pending investigation into claims that he forged a Covid certificate.

The Sunderland star was accused of obtaining a forged vaccination certificate for a doctor based in Lucerne in order to bypass travel restrictions. He later apologised and confirmed his actions were a result of “fear and uncertainty” and a “deep mistrust” in the vaccine, and received a suspended fine of £136,265 (150,000 Swiss francs) from the Lucerne public prosecutor's office. He voluntarily missed all four of Switzerland’s Nations League fixtures.

However, with the matter resolved, he was reinstated to Murat Yakin’s squad for their final two Nations League fixtures, including their clash with Scotland at the AFG Arena on Monday, November 16.

Needing just a point from their game against Slovenia in Maribor this Friday to confirm their status as Group B1 winners, it was hoped that their legendary captain could return to the national fold for the first time since their 3-1 extra-time defeat to Argentina in the World Cup during the summer.

However, on the eve of his side returning for their initial training camp, Xhaka’s absence has been confirmed by national team following a scan at the Academy of Light after he limped out of Sunderland’s win on Sunday afternoon. Revealing the news via a short statement, the Swiss FA said: “Granit Xhaka has to withdraw from the national team gathering due to a calf injury.”

#1959. Arsenal transfer news: Mikel Arteta reveals "valuable" role amid Antonio Nusa links to Gunners ahead of January window

By Lewis Nolan | 07 Nov 2026 15:22

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta has revealed that international matches are used to help assess potential transfer targets amid links to Antonio Nusa.

The RB Leipzig winger has often been touted as a possible target of the Gunners, especially as the Londoners have at times looked blunt in the final third.

With the international break beginning after this weekend, the 21-year-old will be back in action for Norway, and he will play alongside Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard.

Speaking to reporters ahead of their Premier League clash with Hull City on Saturday, Arteta insisted that international matches can be informative when making transfer decisions, saying: "Yes, we do [use international football to aid work ahead of a transfer window].

"Obviously, when we have the opportunity to talk to our players about some players that they share two or three weeks together with, it's very valuable information. I think we all do that. It is a big difference between the Premier League and international football and what is there, but there's always a lot to learn."

Nusa has been included in the Norway squad for his nation's games against Wales on November 14 and against Demark on November 17, and perhaps Odegaard could help convince the winger to move to the Emirates in that time.

Nusa is enjoying a strong season in Germany, with the winger currently Leipzig's leading scorer (six) and assist provider (seven) in all competitions.

His return in both categories have already surpassed the five goals and four assists he produced in 2025-26, and his pace has proven deadly when cutting inside onto his right foot from the left flank.

It is rare for an attacker to be as strong at finishing as they are at creating chances, so Nusa's profile could be invaluable against deep defences.

While he is likely to be expensive in either the January or summer transfer windows, Arsenal should have him high on their radar.

Arsenal have at times been criticised for their style of play, with opposition fans and pundits arguing that they lack attacking intent.

However, it should be remembered that Arteta does not have a particularly elite set of forwards to choose from, with there question marks about every attacker's place in the lineup.

While Nusa may take time to settle into the Premier League, the prospect of Arsenal improving their frontline should be a worry for the rest of the division given the Gunners are already one of the best defensive teams in the world.

Enzo Maresca has made a total of three changes to his Manchester City starting lineup for this evening’s Premier League clash against Nottingham Forest at the City Ground.

Doku will start in his favoured left-wing position, forcing Iliman Ndiaye to move over to the right flank, while Rayan Cherki continues in the number 10 role behind striker Erling Haaland, who is without a goal in his last four appearances against Forest.

As for Nottingham Forest, under-pressure head coach Oliver Glasner has made just two changes to the side that began the 2-0 defeat at Brentford last weekend.

Captain Ryan Yates is handed his first start of the season, with the midfielder replacing Dan Ndoye, while Daniel Munoz is fit to start and comes in for Ola Aina at right wing-back.

Yates is expected to start in the middle of the pitch alongside Xaver Schlager and James McAtee, with the latter potentially given the license to roam further forward to link up with Morgan Gibbs-White.

Munoz and Neco Williams will provide the width in Glasner’s side as wing-backs, while Murillo, Nikola Milenkovic and Jair Cunha will continue in a three-man backline protecting goalkeeper Matz Sels.

“It's just about putting results together and hopefully we go there, [put in a ]good performance and [get] a good result.”

Yoganathan’s start to the season was delayed by injury but he has been firing on all cylinders of late. He has been deployed out on the right flank, where he has proven to be quite the nuisance for defenders.

The former Liverpool academy prospect said: “It feels like with all the hard work beginning to hopefully pay off, especially on a personal note as well, being injured, hopefully we start to kick on now.

“I've worked on my shooting a lot and trying to finish and get in the right areas. I think it was just a lot of my preparation coming off and working, so I'm just really grateful for that.

“I think everyone, especially the first half, probably really enjoyed it. We were getting a lot of joy just running forwards, playing forwards, whether that was down the left or down the right or switching it and then crossing into the box. I think three of our first four goals were crosses, so I think that's something we can look at and work on and move forwards with.

“I was a little bit disappointed I didn't get my third, but we won and that's the main thing.”

#1950. Crystal Palace vs. Liverpool: Bradley Barcola makes Mo Salah claim as "problem" of £100m price tag discussed by Reds winger

By Lewis Nolan | 07 Nov 2026 16:32

Bradley Barcola has waved away concerns about his transfer fee and insisted that he is not trying to replace Mohamed Salah at Liverpool.

The Reds will play their final game before the start of the international break on Sunday, when they take on Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park.

Winger Barcola will hope to score his first Premier League goal of the season, particularly after he received criticism for his performance against Arsenal on November 1.

The forward was was signed for more than £100m in the summer, and many fans have been frustrated by his inconsistent displays, especially as he arrived in the same window that saw Salah leave Anfield after nine years.

Speaking to Sky Sports, Barcola distanced himself from his price tag and suggestions that he is Salah's replacment, saying: "First of all, I wasn't the one who decided the transfer fee, so that's not been my problem.

"Regarding Mo Salah, he's a legend here. A huge one. He's done big things here and for that I have an enormous respect for him, but it's not pressure for me at all.

"I'm not Mohamed Salah, so I'm going to try to contribute whatever I can to the club and make my own mark on its history. I don't feel any pressure about that."

Barcola predominantly plays on the opposite flank to Salah, so perhaps comparisons between the two were not entirely fair.

Asking Barcola to replicate the impact of Salah at Liverpool would be unfair given the latter ended his time in the Premier League as one of the greatest ever players in the competition's history.

The Egyptian ranks as the league's fourth highest scorer of all time (193), while also having produced the joint sixth most assists of all time (94).

Barcola possesses immense qualities of his own, with the Frenchman arguably the fastest player in the division, and he has shown that he can regularly produce shots in the final third.

However, he is more reliant on service than Salah, so Iraola must find ways of getting the 24-year-old the ball more quickly in order for pundits to stop talking about his price tag.

Liverpool will likely field Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Barcola together against Palace, with the trio setting the Reds back in the region of £350m.

Prices across Europe have inflated significantly in recent years, so Liverpool should not necessarily be criticised for the fees they paid for each individual player.

Having said that, the Merseysiders can be criticised for failing to build a functioning attacking unit despite their outlay given the only forwards to have played consistently well this season have been Isak and Rio Ngumoha.

Boss Andoni Iraola inherited a dysfunctional team, but while he has improved the Reds from a defensive perspective, he is unlikely to get Liverpool into a title fight unless he can find a way of extracting more from the club's most expensive assets.

The Gunners striker was controversially pulled back in the penalty area in the first half against Hull City on Saturday afternoon, with the forward expecting a penalty.

Despite referee Farai Hallam was sent over to look at the incident by VAR, though an apparent offside offence saw Mikel Arteta's hopes of claiming a penalty waved away.

While there was controversy about the decision for Havertz's offside position to take precedence over the foul, the fact that the German was ahead of play was concerning.

15 - Kai Havertz has been caught offside 15 times in the Premier League this season, already more than any Arsenal player was flagged in the competition last term (Bukayo Saka, 14). Strayed. https://t.co/QkneG5oDNh

Havertz should not necessarily be criticised for trying to make runs in behind defences, but he is not suited to that role in the team.

Arsenal substituted Viktor Gyokeres on for the 27-year-old in the second half, and while the Swede often makes selfless runs, his return in the final third has been poor.

Similar concerns were raised about the pair in 2025-26, and it has become clear that neither should be Arteta's starting nine next season.

#1943. O'Neill reiterates support for Trusty as Celtic boss slams McAvennie's comments about defender's absence

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 17:48 EST, 4 November 2026

Martin O'Neill has stressed that Auston Trusty has the full backing of everyone at Celtic — after describing Frank McAvennie’s comments about the defender’s ongoing absence as being ‘in poor taste’.

Trusty remains with his family in the US on compassionate grounds following the recent passing of his father Walt.

Speaking on his Let me be Frank podcast this week, former Parkhead striker McAvennie questioned why Trusty wasn’t back playing — describing it as ‘nonsense’ perpetuated by ‘the woke brigade’.

‘I’ve got every respect for that, but how long do you want off?’ McAvennie said. ‘Martin (O’Neill) says he’s away to celebrate the life of his dad.

‘Celebrate the life? You’ve got football. You’re getting paid and we’re in trouble. How long is it going to be?

‘It’s the woke brigade now, isn’t it? It’s nonsense. My dad was the best man, the only man I looked up to when he died, but you’ve got to get on with it.’

Trusty has missed Celtic's last four games after returning home following his father's passing

Those remarks brought a huge backlash with McAvennie later forced into a public apology, claiming he meant no disrespect to Trusty or his family.

‘I should have chosen my words more carefully,’ said McAvennie, who scored 37 goals in 85 games across two spells with Celtic. ‘I can understand why people feel my comments were insensitive. Everyone deals with grief differently and I certainly meant no disrespect.

‘Celtic need the big man back and that’s what I was clumsily trying to say. I wish him and his family all the very best.’

Evidently unimpressed with that attempt to backtrack, O’Neill made it clear that his player, who’s been absent for four matches — against Celta Vigo, Hibernian, Dundee United and Falkirk — should take all the time he needs before returning to Glasgow.

‘That’s really poor taste. That’s really poor,’ said the Celtic boss. ‘I know I’ve said some things and ended up backtracking. But that’s a family bereavement.

‘And that’s making someone’s mind up about how long they should be grieving and stuff like this here. That’s not on.

‘Trusty asked me for some time (off). Even if it’s a celebration (of his late father’s life) it doesn’t matter.

McAvennie has been widely criticised for comments he made on his podcast

‘The father’s been in poor health for quite some considerable time. And I know there was a stage where he thought that he wasn’t going to see it through.

‘But I’m with Trusty the whole way there. Because I wouldn’t want anybody to tell me that I had to grieve over a brother or sister dying. And I’ve had that.

‘He’s 28 years of age. And he’s taken it badly. He has taken it badly. Honestly.

‘I’ve afforded him all the time he wants.

‘At some stage, obviously, he’ll come back. But, at the end of the day, I’ve given that time because I know that we might be talking about different eras or whatever the case may be. That’s nothing to do with it.

‘This is a family thing. And that’s not right.

‘So, Trusty has got the time and he’s got the backing of myself and he’s got the backing of the club.’

The Citizens also conceded early goals against Villa (sixth minute) and against Brighton (11th minute), and it will be difficult to challenge Arsenal unless they can stop going behind in the opening stages of matches.

Manchester City have conceded in the opening 11 minutes of three consecutive games in the Premier League: 6' v Aston Villa ❌ 11' v Brighton ❌ 6' v Nottingham Forest ❌ https://t.co/m5bL7cfO5G

When teams consistently concede in the opening stages of matches, it suggests that there could be a mentality issue at play.

After the Citizens won three of their first four games following confirmation that they had been found guilty by an independent panel in September for breaching the Premier League's financial rules on an industrial scale, Maresca was able to swat aside suggestions that his team would be impacted negatively.

City have since lost three times and won twice, though one of those victories was an EFL Cup triumph against Brighton on penalties.

Maresca's side have also conceded at least two goals in six of the nine games since the October international break ended, and there are clearly severe issues for the head coach to address.

The good news for City is that Arsenal face a difficult fixture schedule in the Premier League after the November international break, with the Gunners set to play Newcastle United, the Citizens, Brentford, Tottenham Hotspur, Bournemouth and Manchester United.

Maresca's side arguably boast an easy next six games in the league, with the club set to face Fulham, Arsenal, Leeds United, Brentford, Chelsea and Hull City.

It remains to be seen if City can rediscover form, and if they fail to stop conceding early, then they could soon find themselves in a battle for top four.

#1938. Man City injury news: Enzo Maresca issues Marc Guehi, Josko Gvardiol update after Nottingham Forest defeat

By Oliver Thomas | 07 Nov 2026 20:48

Enzo Maresca has provided an update on the fitness of Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol following Manchester City’s 3-1 defeat at Nottingham Forest in the Premier League on Saturday.

Both defenders were handed starts in a four-man City backline that conceded twice in the opening 18 minutes courtesy of sloppy mistakes.

Gvardiol was dispossessed from a central position by Jair Cunha who then slotted home Forest’s early opener, before Guehi and Ruben Dias could not prevent powerhouse Liam Delap from barnstorming through on goal and firing the hosts further in front.

Guehi - under fire for recent error-strewn performances - and Gvardiol were then replaced at half time by Nico O'Reilly and Matheus Nunes, and six minutes after the interval, Rayan Cherki rifled the ball into the top corner to give City a glimmer of hope.

However, Forest regained their two-goal cushion thanks to a stunning strike from man-of-the-match Delap, condemning Man City to their third successive Premier League defeat.

Explaining why both Guehi and Gvardiol were withdrawn at half time, Maresca told Sky Sports: "Both injury, both asked for change.

“Marc Guehi [has an] injury and Josko Gvardiol had some issues already during the week, so it was just because they had problems.”

Guehi and Gvardiol were called up to the England and Croatia squads respectively earlier this week ahead of two UEFA Nations League fixtures in November’s international break.

England welcome Croatia to Wembley on November 12 for their penultimate League A Group 3 match, while the Three Lions face Spain and the Checkered Ones take on Czechia in their final game three days later.

However, both Guehi and Gvardiol have now emerged as injury doubts, with an update on their unspecified problems likely to come at the start of next week.

Man City currently have Antoine Semenyo sidelined with a knee injury, with the attacker targeting a return at some stage next month.

O’Reilly, meanwhile, played the second half against Forest but is ‘not 100%’ and has subsequently been left out of Thomas Tuchel’s England squad.

Man City's defensive frailties are a growing concern for Maresca, who highlighted his team's lack of intensity and failure to win duels as major factors behind their disappointing defeat at the City Ground.

“I will speak quite clearly. In the first half when you do not match the intensity and lose all the duels, it is difficult. Then we want to react but it is too late,” Maresca told reporters.

“In these kinds of matches, first of all you need to match the intensity and win the duels. Otherwise it is always complicated.

“In the first half we were not good enough in terms of duels and second balls, we lost all of them.

“Then when we tried to react, we were 2-0 down and in football it is always complicated.

“The first goal we are trying to play and build up. It can happen. It’s the second one, we lost duels in the middle of the pitch, the third one we lost duels in the edge of the box. We don’t need to wait to concede two to react.”

Man City, who are in danger of slipping to third in the Premier League table, are next in action on November 21 at home to Fulham.

#1936. Crystal Palace 1-3 Liverpool: Florian Wirtz on target as Eagles hit rock-bottom in Premier League

Florian Wirtz scored his first Premier League goal of the season as Liverpool beat struggling Crystal Palace 3-1 at Selhurst Park.

Under-pressure Eagles boss Pierre Sage’s side showed promise in the first half, when they had a goal chalked off for offside, hit the crossbar, and forced Alisson Becker into several good saves.

But it was the familiar manner in which they conceded the 40th-minute opener to Alexis Mac Allister – from a set-piece – and after a promising spell, that would have especially frustrated Sage.

Wirtz, whose last Premier League goal came against the same opponents in April, doubled the Reds’ advantage nine minutes into the second half.

Alexander Isak added to the visitors’ lead in the 89th minute, but Andoni Iraola’s side were denied a clean sheet after Eddie Nketiah scored a stoppage-time penalty.

The visitors got to work quickly, calling Dean Henderson into a low save with a Mac Allister effort in the first minute.

But Palace soon enjoyed a brief spell deep in the Liverpool half, where Tyrick Mitchell delivered a ball into the six-yard box but Jorgen Strand Larsen could not angle himself to truly pose a threat to Alisson.

Action returned to Palace’s final third, where Mac Allister attempted to fire home from a free-kick and Dominik Szoboszlai forced a diving stop from Henderson, though the ball looked to be travelling wide.

Yeremy Pino went agonisingly close to opening the scoring in the 18th minute. The crowd rose in anticipation after the Spain international collected Mitchell’s cross, then curled an effort – which looked to have Alisson beaten – off the crossbar.

Pino had little time to rue the fine margins, as he was then called back into action from a corner, rising highest to meet it but directing it at the Brazil keeper for a straightforward save.

#1935. Celtic hierarchy deserve credit for fronting up at fan meeting... but the toughest questions still lie ahead for beleaguered boss Martin O'Neill

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 17:53 EST, 4 November 2026

It says much about where Celtic are as a club right now that very little of Martin O’Neill’s pre-match press conference actually centred on the match in question.

Just in case you hadn’t heard, Turkish giants Besiktas are in town for a game which the Parkhead men surely must win to stand any chance of progressing in the Europa League.

Their squad contains former Celtic striker Oh Hyeon-gyu and ex-Arsenal midfielder Leandro Trossard. For added spice, how about former Rangers’ defender Ridvan Yilmaz playing left-back, or Vaclav Cerny, a man who once squirted water at Celtic supporters, being their right-winger?

Their manager, Vincenzo Italiano, also happened to oversee Bologna in January as O’Neill’s men emerged with a draw from a fiery encounter on the road.

On another day, those plot lines would have dominated the agenda. Yet they were relegated to mere footnotes as a consequence of Celtic’s seemingly inexorable lurch towards crisis point.

Bluntly, the identity of the side which will seek to inflict a record fifth consecutive European defeat on their team is of little concern right now to the green and white hordes. They only see a side which is regressing and a manager and a backroom staff who seem incapable of arresting the slide.

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill is hoping a much-needed win in Europe can help lift the gloom

More significantly, in the wider picture, they view the hierarchy as being devoid of the necessary ambition or footballing intelligence to turn the tanker around. The lack of scrutiny the directors have subjected themselves to as matters have steadily deteriorated on their watch is another major bugbear.

Purely taken in isolation, then, it’s hard to be critical of the fact that some of those suited figures – plus O’Neill – voluntarily put themselves through a ‘hard but fair’ questioning at Greenock Celtic Supporters’ Club on Monday evening.

‘When things are going really well at the football club, you can take all the plaudits and all that you want,’ said the manager. ‘At the end of the day, there are bad times and I think that you should face up to that.’

O’Neill, to be clear, wasn’t on the original list to attend. Once he heard of the event, he made it his business to be there.

While he could have lived without a balaclava-clad welcoming committee, he felt the exercise was largely positive.

‘First of all, I wasn’t really aware of the meeting, so it was kind of an ad hoc thing,’ he explained.

‘I spoke to Michael (Nicholson, chief executive) and he said that they were going to meet. And I said, “Well, I wouldn’t mind going down to it if that was the case”, obviously to experience what the fans would be asking.

Falkirk's defeat of the champions last weekend has seen a wave of criticism hit the Celtic boss

‘I don’t know whether they expected me to be there or not, but it doesn’t really matter. Regardless of who was there, the meeting itself was robust with strong, strong questioning.

‘Hopefully, some of the answers would maybe quell if not satisfy. I don’t know what the overall picture would be. But, yeah, I was pleased to have gone.’

Accused of adopting the public profiles of Invisible Men throughout this year, the presence of Nicholson, Chris McKay and Brian Wilson in Inverclyde became instantly newsworthy.

With the divide between the boardroom and fans apparently widening by the week, even hardened cynics viewed the trip to the Tail O’ The Bank as a small step in the right direction.

With the AGM on the horizon, the hope is that the meeting might just lead to a more civilised discourse going forward.

By all accounts, the questions asked on every subject from recruitment to the hoarding of cash were answered as fully as possible. But no one on the floor left the building clicking their heels at what the future holds. Talk is cheap, after all.

‘If the takeaway was that the board were going to do something to satisfy the supporters in that sense, then that would be great,’ added O’Neill. ‘That would be brilliant for all.’

Angry Celtic supporters continue to make their feelings clear on the club's board every week

By sheer chance, O’Neill was scheduled to attend a Q&A with supporters when he first returned to the club last year. A Celtic legend as a consequence of his exploits at the turn of the century, those present stopped just short of carrying him in a sedan chair.

After just three wins in ten games, the mood music around him was a little less jovial in Greenock.

For perhaps the first time in his long association with the club, adverse results have seen a spotlight shine on him.

‘That’s the course of a football season or the experiences of a football club,’ he shrugged. ‘I think sometimes you have to put a few things into perspective, both good and bad. And I think the other night was one of those, you know?

‘People are asking me now if it’s something I’m going to continue to do. No, my main job depends on results and winning some football matches. That’s the most important thing.’

Back in the day, criticism over such a wretched run would have been limited to newspaper columns and radio phone-ins. In the modern era, the level of flak is amplified by the proliferation of podcasts and blogs from citizen journalists.

‘I have never been immune to that,’ O’Neill insisted. ‘Listen, everyone would love to be praised every single minute of your life. But that’s not going to happen. You’ve got to forget about the noise and try and get on with it and get back to winning ways.

Former Celtic striker Oh Hyeon-gyu will lead the line for Besiktas at Parkhead on Thursday

‘Everyone is a tactician now, that’s the whole point. Everybody is a football manager. There are people who have got jobs in football now because they played a PlayStation. Honestly, it’s extraordinary. But it does not bother me, honestly, it doesn’t.

‘People talk about tactics, but in my semi-defence, no one talked about tactics when we won the seven games to win the league. Or the 14 games we won before we got beat.

‘And you know what? If you got beaten in a game, you think that maybe that somebody has out-thought you. Absolutely. You’re right to think that.

‘John McGlynn has every right to be proud of his (Falkirk) side after beating us and to have had the upper hand.’

O’Neill, unusually, has got used to losing lately, with seven reverses coming by the first week in November. But, as those in attendance on Monday or when he appeared in Dingwall for a B team game the following night will attest, he’s not lost his desire to lead or to win. He remains all-in.

‘I really have to be, honestly, because I’m supposed to be the driver of the club,’ he stated.

‘For instance, last night (Tuesday), that was wildly important for me to go up to that game (in Dingwall). I feel that that’s my job at the end of the day.’

#1933. Sunderland 1-0 Chelsea: Blues pay the penalty as Enzo Le Fee lifts Black Cats off foot of Premier League table

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Sunderland ended their winless run in the Premier League with a hard-fought 1-0 win over Chelsea at the Stadium of Light.

The Black Cats entered Sunday’s game on a worrying run of form, with Thursday night’s Europa League loss to Dinamo Zagreb the latest setback, but an energetic first-half display against the Blues was rewarded when Enzo Le Fee scored from the penalty spot.

Chelsea enjoyed the bulk of possession after the break but struggled to make it count as they slipped to a fourth league defeat of the season and dropped out of the top four.

Victory ended a long winless run for Sunderland, who had last taken three points in the Premier League against Fulham back in August. They remain in the relegation zone but at least climbed off the foot of the table.

Regis Le Bris made eight changes from the Dinamo defeat, which included a first league start of the season for Chemsdine Talbi, while Chelsea made two switches from last weekend’s win over Manchester United as former Black Cat Jordan Henderson started.

Sunderland were handed a blow just four minutes into the match when captain Granit Xhaka was forced off and Jules Ahoka came on.

An even-paced start saw Ahoka win the ball and play Talbi through. The winger’s cross was met by Trai Hume, who had a hooked strike blocked by the defence.

Talbi was at the heart of another promising chance, sending in a great cross for Brian Brobbey, who volleyed wide.

At the other end Cole Palmer charged into the area and was bundled over, but a VAR check deemed contact happened outside the box.

Morgan Rogers then came close to opening the scoring when his powerful header from close-range flew wide.

#1932. Tottenham to lodge 'formal complaint' over Jayden Bogle VAR decision after Mathys Tel injury update

By Ben Knapton | 07 Nov 2026 22:23

Tottenham Hotspur reportedly intend to complain to Pro Ref after Leeds United's Jayden Bogle controversially escaped a red card in Saturday's Premier League clash.

Spurs' top-flight revival was nipped in the bud in a 1-0 loss to Leeds at Elland Road, where Noah Okafor struck the decisive goal for Daniel Farke's side in the second half.

However, Tottenham were aggrieved that the game finished 11 versus 11, as Leeds right-back Bogle caught Mathys Tel on the back of his ankle with a dreadful studs-up challenge in the first half.

Referee John Brooks did not deem the incident punishment-worthy at the time, though, while VAR official Tony Harrington elected not to send the on-field official to the monitor either, determining that Bogle had not committed serious foul play.

The PL Match Centre on X released a transcript of the audio conversation between Harrington and Brooks, the former declaring that Bogle's tackle amounted to reckless rather than dangerous.

"I'm confirming the on-field decision of no red card. There’s a lack of speed going into the challenge and he’s stepping into the tackle. Confirming a reckless challenge," Harrington said.

Should Jason Bogle have seen red for this challenge? ?? ? Stream live on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/fuK42Okkcz

However, BBC Sport states that Tottenham will lodge a formal complaint with the referees' body, as the Lilywhites unsurprisingly believe that Bogle should have been made to take the walk of shame.

Spurs will seek an explanation from Pro Ref as to why Bogle was allowed to stay on the pitch, although De Zerbi refused to criticise the officials and technology in his post-game interview.

"We have full confidence in the referee and VAR. I cannot say nothing more," De Zerbi told BBC Match of the Day, as Spurs suffered their fourth loss of the Premier League season.

The North London giants nevertheless remain in the top half of the Premier League table, although they will drop back down into the bottom 10 if either Ipswich Town or Aston Villa collect a point on Sunday.

Tel was unable to carry on after feeling the full force of Bogle's studs, and the Frenchman had to be replaced by Dominic Solanke with 43 minutes gone at Elland Road.

De Zerbi had no positive news to share on Tel's condition at full time, suggesting that the Frenchman is set for a spell on the sidelines.

"Bad injury and now we have to make the medical check, and the next day we will know what is the problem," De Zerbi told reporters in his post-game press conference.

Tel was called up to the France Under-21 squad for November's fixtures against Italy and England, but the former Bayern Munich man will now almost certainly have to pull out of the selection.

Tel has scored one goal in 10 games so far this season for Tottenham, whose first game back after the international break comes at home to Ipswich Town on November 21.

#1930. Romano: Milan remain obsessed with Inacio but Fonseca’s arrival could change things

It’s no secret that AC Milan will sign a defender in January, and one name is sitting firmly in the lead but he’s not alone.

Since the summer, Milan have been obsessed with the idea of signing Goncalo Inacio. His name was constant through the mercato and on deadline day, the Rossoneri tried to pounce on a last-minute deal. However, it was unsuccessful, understandably.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Within days of the mercato shutting, the Rossoneri were linked with another move in the January window and these suggestions have not gone away in the months since. Other names have been suggested, but again, Inacio remains the priority.

Speaking on his YouTube channel today, Fabrizio Romano offered an update on the club’s pursuit for Inacio ahead of the January mercato, via MilanNews.

“A defender will definitely arrive. He was supposed to arrive in the summer; he will arrive in January, so it’s no mystery. Milan also persistently sought him during the summer transfer window, an extra defender obviously in addition to Mario Gila, who was also an excellent investment by Milan, so the idea is to bring in at least another one.

“Milan reinstated Tomori a minute after the end of the summer transfer window out of necessity, but Milan’s idea is to take an extra defender. So a defender will definitely arrive.

“The name of Gonçalo Inácio must always be kept there because it is a name that has been in Milan’s mind since the first day of the summer transfer window; from when Ruben Amorim arrived until the last minute of the transfer window, he has always been in the thoughts anyway. There have been different attempts with different formulas.

“Milan had even considered, at a certain point at the end of August, a possible very expensive loan with an option to buy, so several solutions were considered that Sporting did not accept.

“Among other things, Sporting has changed its skin; Paolo Fonseca arrived on the bench, so we’ll see how much this will impact the dynamics of this operation. Clearly he’s not the only name, but Inacio is certainly a very welcome player; Milan has excellent relations with his agents, who are the same as Amorim.

“But I repeat, it doesn’t end here; there’s a list and Milan will make their choices.”

It’s a positive start that a defender will ‘definitely’ arrive; it’s just a case of whether they’re the right man now with Inacio not seeming like the definitive candidate.

#1929. Xabi Alonso knows he has at least one Chelsea dependable

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

When Emmanuel Emegha came on in the 87th minute to join Danny Welbeck up front, the only surprising thing, as Chelsea got desperate in their bid to save themselves at the last at Sunderland, was that it was Jordan Henderson to make way.

Henderson was unlikely to provide the goal threat Chelsea needed in those dying embers of Sunday’s eventual 1-0 defeat, but he had increasingly been the free man and the right passing option for whoever in yellow and black had the ball at their feet as the match had gone on.

A defeat at the Stadium of Light to the side who had begun the day at the bottom of the Premier League table was a grim result for Xabi Alonso’s team to head into the international break with, especially given it was reminiscent of the 3-0 loss at Brentford ahead of the last hiatus.

Chelsea were devoid of ideas and lacking any semblance of the sort of control Alonso has publicly called for from his players.

And yet whatever it is about his team that is failing to give him that control and dominance right now, the problem is to be found elsewhere than where Henderson is going about his business.

Though they won last weekend against Manchester United without him, his return at Sunderland following illness was a welcome one. A midfield of Moises Caicedo plus either Romeo Lavia or Henderson or both, as was deployed on Sunday, is just about the only thing functioning as it should be for Chelsea right now.

For Henderson personally, it was a full-circle afternoon in the North East. Henderson is Sunderland born and bred and his appearance was significant. It was for Sunderland, against Chelsea, that 18 years and seven days earlier he had made his senior debut. Now came the 700th appearance, donning the colours of the visiting team.

Chelsea pay the penalty in latest defeat to Sunderland

Choose the right education path for your child

The visitors faltered. With a controversial penalty given against them and Cole Palmer contentiously not awarded one of his own, Palmer and Morgan Rogers both had off-days, Levi Colwill was deemed expendable enough to be substituted at half-time, and none of Alonso’s substitutions could force the issue and muster an equaliser.

Henderson was sensible in possession when others around him were not

Henderson, though, was sensible in possession when others around him were not. He kept the ball moving, with one-touch passes into feet, relieving the pressure Chelsea were under in one of English football’s more hostile grounds.

Alonso won all five games against Sunderland as a Liverpool player and scored the winner in one of them, yet no such Midas touch in Chelsea colours from the technical area this time. His Chelsea gave Sunderland their first win in eight Premier League matches.

Winning blockbuster battles against the so-called ‘big six’ is important, but Premier League titles are won and European places earned by finding consistency, by winning home and away against the Sunderlands, Hulls and Fulhams of the Premier League.

Chelsea are yet to reach that point, as Henderson — who spent years in Liverpool teams that could and did — will be all too aware. The 36-year-old is not the problem. He actually represents what there is that’s working.

#1928. JJ Gabriel reveals key motivation behind Real Madrid transfer after Man Utd exit

JJ Gabriel has revealed the key motivation behind his impending move to Real Madrid after turning his back on Manchester United.

Gabriel, who turned 16 on October 6, informed United of his desire to leave in September and has not trained with the club since then.

The young forward has attracted interest from several clubs across Europe, but has now reached a verbal agreement to join Real Madrid.

The forward joined United’s academy four years ago and quickly established himself as one of the most highly-rated youngsters at the club, featuring for the U18 side at the age of just 14.

Gabriel played under Michael Carrick during the club’s pre-season camp, but his entourage are understood to have grown unhappy with his first-team integration and playing opportunities at United.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

The teenager, who has an Irish passport, could finalise a move to the Spanish giants as early as January next year, with United reportedly set to receive £350,000 in compensation.

And in a brief interview with the Spanish outlet Marca, Gabriel revealed he has one particular goal in mind for his time at Real.

‘My dream is to win a Ballon d’Or,’ he said.

When asked about a potential move to Barcelona instead, Gabriel simply responded: ‘Obviously, Madrid.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

A move to Real is a bold step at such a young age, and United legend Ryan Giggs believes Gabriel may have been better served following the example of Max Dowman, whose development is not being rushed by Arsenal or Mikel Arteta.

📰🔜 JJ Gabriel with Marca’s front page confirming the move to Real Madrid is close: “Can I keep this [newspaper] with me?”. pic.twitter.com/cerdxXsbE4

‘So far in his career everything is going fine, why would you disrupt that? You’re on the right track,’ Giggs said of Gabriel on Rio Ferdinand Presents.

‘I trained at 15, I didn’t play for the first team until two years later so you have to have that patience that people just don’t seem to have at the moment.

‘And believe it or not, first-team football for Man United is completely different to playing in the youth team, playing pre-season for the first team, it’s completely different. That first game, yeah, you might do alright, but you have to do it for 40, 50 games a season. You’re going to get injuries, loss of form, bad results, so you have to be patient.

‘If you’re on the right trajectory then just bide your time, no matter how good you are.

‘Max Dowman is unbelievable but he’s not playing for Arsenal at the moment.

‘I’m sure he’ll bide his time, I’m sure he’s getting impatient, but he’s not kicking off, he knows in a couple of years time he might be the main man for Arsenal.’

#1927. Man United sink to new 40-year low after Nottingham Forest beat Man City

By Ben Knapton | 07 Nov 2026 22:41

Manchester United have sunk to a new 40-year low thanks to Nottingham Forest's shock victory over Manchester City on Saturday evening.

Ahead of the start of gameweek 10, the Red Devils were just about keeping their heads above water in the Premier League table, sitting outside the relegation zone on goal difference.

Michael Carrick's men led Crystal Palace by that metric, while sitting two points clear of rock-bottom Sunderland and one better off than Forest after nine rounds.

The Tricky Trees were unsurprisingly tipped to suffer defeat to Enzo Maresca's men at the City Ground, but in an unexpected turn of events, Forest claimed a 3-1 triumph on home soil.

Jair Cunha and Liam Delap propelled the Garibaldi into a 2-0 lead before Rayan Cherki pulled one back, but the Frenchman's response was futile as Delap struck his second of the game in the second half.

Forest's win propelled Oliver Glasner's men out of the Premier League drop zone, while simultaneously forcing Man United into the bottom three, two points adrift of 17th-placed Coventry City.

The Red Devils therefore find themselves in the bottom three after nine rounds for the first time since November 1986, when they were in 21st place after 15 games of the 1986-87 season.

November 1986 was the same month that Ron Atkinson was dismissed and Sir Alex Ferguson took over as head coach, and the latter ultimately led Man Utd to an 11th-placed finish in the First Division.

The 20-time English champions will rise to 16th place if they beat Aston Villa by any scoreline on Sunday, though, while victory by three goals or more will also lift them above Fulham into 15th spot.

Nevertheless, Carrick remains a man under major pressure after Man United's new 40-year worst, in spite of Tuesday's extraordinary 3-2 Champions League comeback triumph over Roma.

Man United always intended to get to the November international break before making any firm managerial decisions, so to say Carrick bought himself more time with Tuesday's fightback may be inaccurate.

However, another pitiful Premier League performance and result on Sunday could force the hierarchy to take action, especially with the current bookies' favourites available for hire immediately.

The odds on Eddie Howe replacing Carrick are now as low as 8/13 on some operators, while Julian Nagelsmann is the second-favourite to take charge at 11/4.

Antonio Conte and Unai Emery are not far behind, the latter's links with Old Trafford representing a fascinating sub-plot ahead of tomorrow's fixture.

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso and goalkeeper Mike Penders disagree over Sunderland’s match-winning penalty.

The Blues suffered a painful 1-0 defeat to Sunderland on Sunday, losing to the team that began the day rooted to the foot of the Premier League table.

Enzo Le Fee scored the only goal of the game from the penalty spot after Levi Colwill was controversially adjudged to have fouled Brian Brobbey when tussling with the Dutch striker as he ran towards goal.

#1924. Alisson FUMES at Liverpool team-mate Jeremy Jacquet after Reds star turned his back and deflected Mason Greenwood's free-kick beyond goalkeeper

Published: 14:15 EST, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 18:19 EST, 4 November 2026

Alisson is usually composure personified for Liverpool but lost his rag with Jeremy Jacquet on Wednesday night.

The Brazilian gave his team-mate both barrels after Fenerbahce's equaliser - a heavily deflected Mason Greenwood free-kick.

Jacquet was at the edge of the Liverpool wall and twisted his body to take evasive action, with the ball ricocheting off his midriff and past the goalkeeper.

Jacquet has been a shining light for the Reds in his debut campaign but it was a poor moment that left his stopper livid.

Replay footage showed Greenwood's powerful attempt appeared to be heading wide before the deflection off Jacquet completely changed the trajectory.

Alisson had been moving swiftly to his left before being wrong-footed and the ball flew off the wet surface to his other side.

Alisson was raging at Jeremy Jacquet's poor blocking attempt for the Fenerbahce equaliser

Jacquet's expression indicated he knew he'd made a poor mistake for the goal

The 34-year-old's fury was immediate and he screamed at Jacquet, gesticulating wildly in his direction.

The centre-back appeared to recognise his mistake and brought his hand up to cover his eyes on a grim evening in Istanbul.

On commentary for TNT Sports, Ally McCoist said: 'It's Jacquet and he's livid (Alisson), does he turn his back? He certainly does, you've got to face it.

'The goalkeeper is livid, absolutely livid and with justification as well. He's (Jacquet) is side on for someone who has had a good start to the season.'

Jacquet has been partnering Virgil van Dijk in almost every game so far this term for Andoni Iraola's men and acquitted himself excellently.

Having joined from Rennes in the summer for £55million after agreeing the move in January, he's seamlessly replaced Ibrahima Konate, who left on a free transfer before signing for Real Madrid.

Jacquet is still just 21 and the France international will no doubt want to avoid the ire of his goalkeeper and learn his lesson when it comes to forming a solid wall.

Trey Nyoni had opened the scoring for the Reds before Greenwood's leveller. Alexander Isak then came off the bench to give the visitors the lead once more before Fenerbahce roared back.

As reported by The Athletic last week, United hierarchy held talks about Carrick’s future as head coach following the 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth on October 25.

Carrick had been widely expected to be sacked at that point and then again after Man Utd were beaten 2-0 by Chelsea in the Premier League, a result that sent them crashing down the table.

However, it was agreed that Carrick would oversee the Roma and Aston Villa games before his situation would be reassessed prior to the international break.

Now, even though Carrick ended a nine-game run without a victory in thrilling fashion against Roma, pressure still remains as the first half performance on Tuesday night was a disaster and United could have easily found themselves three or four goals down at half-time.

Of course, the second half did prove that the players are playing for Carrick, so much so that Matheus Cunha went overboard in getting himself sent-off after turning the game on its head with two quickfire goals.

There’s an argument that Man Utd now have some much-needed momentum, but the calamitous fashion of Sunday’s 4-4 draw with Aston Villa suggests there is nothing of the sort.

#1916. Why Crystal Palace vs. Liverpool is key for Andoni Iraola's tenure amid Arne Slot comparisons before Premier League clash

By Lewis Nolan | 07 Nov 2026 23:24

Liverpool will take on Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park on Sunday, and a third consecutive defeat would place Andoni Iraola under pressure.

The head coach has so far taken charge of 15 games as Reds boss, and while he has only lost three times, there is growing discontent in some sections of the fanbase.

After losing against Arsenal in the Premier League last weekend and suffering a defeat away to Fenerbahce in the Champions League on Wednesday, there are concerns his position could be in danger if he was to suffer a third consecutive loss on Sunday.

Iraola is also only contracted to Anfield until 2028, so the Merseysiders will have to make a decision about whether to renew his deal sooner rather than later.

Heading into the upcoming international break on the back of three defeats would no doubt place Iraola under further pressure from those that were already sceptical about his appointment.

Here, Sports Mole explains why Iraola could come under extra scrutiny this weekend, while also exploring whether he should be fearful about his future at Liverpool.

One of the reasons that some Liverpool supporters are uneasy about the inconsistencies of the team this season is that they saw the club experience a turbulent 2025-26.

Under the direction of Arne Slot, the Reds finished fifth with just 60 points, and they lost 19 times in all competitions, though their 2025 Community Shield loss takes that number to 20.

Fans were distraught that Liverpool could surrender their Premier League title so easily, and the team's struggles last season created a rift amongst many, with the two camps split over their support of Slot.

The Dutchman's dismissal in May was met with mixed reactions, and the appointment of Iraola was divisive given he was replacing a title-winning manager.

While many fans have acknowledged that the squad the current head coach inherited was flawed, those that backed Slot believe that Iraola has not been held to the same standards as his predecessor.

Liverpool have 15 points so far after nine matchweeks, which is exactly the same tally as they had accumulated after the end of matchweek nine in 2025-26.

However, the Reds claimed just 45 points from their final 33 league games under Slot, with the club fortunate that they won their first five games of that campaign.

The underlying numbers in 2025-26 were alarming, and their final 33 matches extrapolated over a full season would equate to just 52 points, enough to finish 10th last term.

Iraola's side are highly unlikely to be as poor over the remainder of 2026-27, and he deserves the chance to take the squad as far as he can.

Liverpool struggled throughout Slot's final season when pressing, with critiques made of the Dutchman's out of possession approach, as well as fitness conditioning.

Iraola was highly regarded at Rayo Vallecano and Bournemouth for the intensity he demanded from his players, and that same high-energy system has been used at Liverpool to great effect.

The Reds have pressed the likes of Arsenal, Brentford and Bournemouth exceptionally well this term, and they have also looked far more assured at the back.

Liverpool have kept four clean sheets in their past seven league matches, while only conceding once against each of Brentford and Arsenal.

Manchester City may have beaten the Merseysiders 3-0 in early October, but they only managed to open the scoring once Ryan Gravenberch had been sent off.

The introduction of Ronald Araujo has been vital, with the defender essentially acting as a third centre-back at right-back, though the system that the team uses is far more structured without the ball in general

Liverpool were one of the worst clubs in the Premier League last term out of possession, so for the Reds to have improved so significantly in such a short period of time has been impressive.

Despite the undeniable improvements defensively, questions have been raised about how Iraola is platforming the team's attack given the club have scored just 11 goals in the Premier League so far.

Striker Alexander Isak has netted six times in the top flight, though he has had little service so far, and he has performed remarkably well to reach that figure.

The Reds have three £100m attackers in their squad in Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola, with the latter two yet to score in the league this season.

Portions of the fanbase have suggested that Iraola has failed the team's attackers, and considering goals are more eye-catching than defending, the team's struggles in the final third have been more apparent than the development at the other end of the pitch.

However, the head coach cannot be faulted for many of team's difficulties given he inherited Wirtz, who has never shown that he is capable of regularly producing in front of goal.

Liverpool's full-backs on both flanks have offered little threat when going forward regardless of personnel, and the only creative wide player in the squad is winger Rio Ngumoha.

The 18-year-old cannot be expected to play every game, so that has often resulted in blunt performances in attack, and the Merseysiders may not improve offensively without further investment.

Every game requires context before analysing, and even if the Reds lose against Palace on Sunday, it would be harsh to suggest that Iraola should be under pressure.

He has taken over a dysfunctional squad with several gaps, and it would be unfair to argue that he must overcome all of those problems without further transfer windows.

A Liverpool defeat on Sunday would unfortunately amplify his critics, and the November international break could be a long one for the head coach.

Victory for Iraola could take his side as high as fourth, and it would also be the club's 10th triumph in 14 games, a more than respectable return.

#1915. Roy Keane sends message to Manchester United fans after Aston Villa draw

Roy Keane has sent a message to Manchester United fans after Sunday's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa left the club in the Premier League relegation zone.

The build-up to the game at Old Trafford was dominated by speculation over Michael Carrick's future as manager and a planned fan protest against the club ownership.

Green and gold balloons - which are symbolic of the club's past - were seen in the Stretford End and then a banner was unfurled with read: "We don't want a new stadium, we want new owners."

On the pitch, Man Utd found themselves 2-0 down after four minutes, and then 4-2 down before the hour mark, but the players were applauded off by some on Sunday after a thrilling fightback.

Whether the point is enough for Carrick to keep his job remains to be seen, with Man Utd languishing in 18th place in the standings.

But the main focus of the supporters' ire was the Glazers, co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and director of football Jason Wilcox.

Speaking after the game, Keane acknowledged and praised the fans.

"Manchester United fans get criticised a lot, but I think United fans are really fair supporters, I really do," he said on Sky Sports.

"They're fair with the players. We saw at the Bournemouth game the players were getting booed off. They gave them a round of applause here because the players gave a little bit of something back.

"That's the minimum you should be giving the supporters.

#1914. Theo Walcott singles out ‘frustrating’ Arsenal star after Hull City win
