Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Hansi Flick stressed that Barcelona still have a long road ahead of them in their quest to win LaLiga for a third straight season.

Barca went into the international break top of the standings following a 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid on Sunday.

After seeing Real Madrid go level on points after beating Valencia 24 hours earlier, Barca came from behind to win at the Estadio Metropolitano thanks to Fermin Lopez's brace.

Diego Simeone's side, who could have gone top themselves with a win, made the perfect start when Giuliano Simeone finished past Joan Garcia in the 10th minute.

But Barca hit back on the stroke of half-time when Pedri's driving run from deep ended with Fermin superbly sweeping a left-footed finish into the bottom-right corner.

The comeback was completed in the 66th minute by Fermin, who collected Lamine Yamal's defence-splitting pass before scoring to seal a huge three points for the Blaugrana.

Barca's win was made even more impressive given they came up against an Atletico side that had won their last seven LaLiga matches.

The Blaugrana have now won their first six away games in LaLiga 2026-27. It is the third time they have achieved the feat, and the first since 2012-13, when they won the first 10, but Flick is not getting carried away.

#1824. Furious Martin O'Neill hits out at 'debacle' after balaclava-wearing protesters abused Celtic chiefs outside meeting

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 04:56 EST, 5 November 2026

Celtic boss Martin O’Neill has hit out at individuals wearing balaclavas who turned up at a meeting between directors and supporters.

Staged at the Greenock Celtic Supporters’ Club on Monday evening, the event afforded around 120 fans a rare chance to grill the hierarchy on the direction the club is taking.

Chief executive Michael Nicholson, finance director Chris McKay and interim chairman Brian Wilson attended — with O’Neill also venturing along after learning that it was scheduled to take place.

And while the manager was pleased to have participated in a ‘robust’ discussion, he was horrified that those executives who’d agreed to front up were abused by certain fans — believed to be ultras — who hid their faces as they congregated outside.

It’s understood that they weren’t permitted access to the meeting room itself but it was still a worrying sight amid the ongoing unrest surrounding the club, with the threat of more protests ahead of Thursday night's Europa League clash with Besiktas at Celtic Park.

The flashpoint came weeks after Dermot Desmond, the club’s largest shareholder, had tennis balls thrown at him by protesters as he participated in the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship at St Andrews.

‘There was a bit of a debacle beforehand,’ said the Northern Irishman. ‘But the meeting itself was, I think you could use the word robust, yes, firm, but very orderly questioning.

O'Neill admitted he was disappointed to see individuals wearing balaclavas outside meeting

‘(We were) trying to give the answers that (were) not necessarily what people are looking for, because I’m not so sure that will ever reach a satisfactory stage for a while anyway.

‘But, yeah, it was really interesting and an experience.

‘Was everything answered by the board and myself to their satisfaction? Well, you’d have to ask the people there at the time.

‘There was no shouting. It wasn’t like (last year’s) AGM. The shouting had taken place before the meeting, you know? I mean, you are aware that people with balaclavas came up to the thing? To me, I think that was the saddest thing.

‘Would I have ever, in any day, ever thought that Celtic fans would be clothed in balaclavas before a meeting? Even if they were disapproving of what was happening, I think that’s really disappointing.

‘I do find it hard to get my head round that kind of stuff.’

The meeting came amid speculation that the club’s forthcoming annual general meeting would be held remotely.

Last year’s AGM was cut short by then chairman, Peter Lawwell, after it was disrupted by individuals shouting and brandishing red cards.

O'Neill attended  meeting with Celtic fans in Greenock where he said questioning was robust

It’s understood, though, that the meeting will go ahead as normal in a suite at Celtic Park — with O’Neill expecting to attend.

‘That’s early December, isn’t it?’ he asked. ‘So, I would expect to be at it as a manager. I assume that Brendan (Rodgers) was (present previously), so you’d be at it.

‘If given an opportunity to answer some of the things and if they want to hear from the manager, I would have no problem.

‘I hope it’s similar to what Monday night was in terms of the questions and fairness and not falling into what it was last year.’

While no minutes were taken at the meeting in Greenock, there’s been speculation that O’Neill confirmed he’d be leaving the club in the summer — despite a one-year option remaining.

Although he didn’t confirm this on Wednesday, he said: ‘I can’t imagine anybody asking me back. Seriously, I can’t imagine that happening.

‘Listen, I didn’t come in here today to give a final word at this minute.’

#1821. Why Do Football Clubs Let Players Leave for Free?

Why would a club let a valuable player walk out the door for nothing?

Because sometimes nothing is the best offer on the table.

Football clubs may let a player leave for free when the cost or risk of a new contract outweighs the value of keeping him.

A club may also prefer one final season of sporting contribution to a modest transfer fee. Sometimes the player chooses not to renew, while the signing club can still face wages, bonuses and agent fees.

So the word “free” does a lot of heavy lifting in football.

It is the only price tag in the sport that tells you what the selling club gets, and nothing about what the buying club pays.

This guide explains the topic for senior professional football, with examples drawn from English football.

Where FIFA rules and domestic rules part ways, we say so without hesitation.

A free transfer is a move in which no transfer fee is paid to the previous club, commonly because the player’s contract has expired.

When we’re talking about a free agent, we’re talking about an unattached player.

“Free” describes the absence of a transfer fee here. It does not remove wages, signing costs or any compensation that rules may still require.

The word also gets stretched quite a bit.

A contract that runs out on its end date is a free transfer. A deal that both sides agree to end early, called mutual termination, is something else. So is a release, where a club lets a player go while he is still under contract.

Headlines rarely make the distinction, but the rulebook does.

You can compare free signings with fee-paying moves in our confirmed football transfers database.

No sporting director wakes up planning to lose a player for nothing.

It happens when every other option looks worse, which in football is more often than fans like to believe.

Unless a club explains its motive in public (and clubs rarely do), read them as general reasoning, not as the known story behind any specific deal.

A renewal is rarely a copy of the old deal.

It usually comes with a raise, a signing bonus and a fresh agent fee. If the club doubts the player will be worth that money in year three or four, letting the contract expire is the cheaper mistake.

A lengthy contract for an older player can increase a club’s exposure to injury or declining performance.

The club pays the full salary whether the player stays fit or not, and many clubs would rather stop early.

A player who no longer fits still collects his wages, and those wages still count against the club’s spending limits. Loyalty does not have its own line in the accounts.

Sometimes a club lets a contract run out on purpose.

If the best offer is modest, one more season of goals, a title push or a cup run can be worth more than the money.

Fans may call it a blunder in January. By May, some of them call it a trophy.

A club cannot force a renewal and it cannot force a sale either.

If the player turns down every new contract and every move his club agrees, the deal simply runs out. He leaves for free, usually with a better offer already waiting somewhere else.

A short contract gives a club less long-term wage exposure and gives a player an earlier chance to renegotiate or move. It also offers less security to the player and less protection of resale value to the club. The right length depends on performance risk, bargaining power and each side’s plans.

For a club, a two-year deal limits the damage if a signing flops. The price is that the club may be shopping for a replacement sooner than planned.

It protects resale value, because any buyer must pay to take over the years still left. But it turns into an anchor if the player’s form drops, since the wages keep coming whether he plays or not.

Short contracts and free transfers are related, but they are not the same decision.

A short deal moves the end date closer. What happens on that date is a separate argument, usually held in a room full of agents.

Every contract has a clock on it, and the clock usually works for the player.

As a contract approaches expiry, a club will generally have less leverage in transfer negotiations, because the player may become available without a fee.

Is there a formula for how fast that value falls?

Form, demand, injuries and competition among interested clubs can all affect the fee available.

For clubs hoping to recover a transfer fee, an earlier sale or a contract extension may improve their position.

Keeping the player until expiry can still be the better sporting decision.

A player’s value and the cost of signing him are not necessarily the same thing. Transfer fees attract most of the headlines, while wages, signing bonuses and agent payments can be just as important to a club’s finances. Transfer speculation also extends beyond traditional football reporting, with discussions appearing on social media and platforms such as crypto betting site Sportbet.one, although these conversations should not be confused with verified transfer fees or the actual financial terms of a deal.

Before 1995, a player at the end of his contract was not really free.

His old club could still demand a fee before letting him go, and Jean-Marc Bosman, a Belgian midfielder, found that out in 1990.

He was nearing the end of his contract with RFC Liège and rejected a new offer that would have cut his salary by about 75%. He wanted to join French club Dunkerque instead.

The two clubs reached a conditional transfer agreement, but Liège doubted Dunkerque’s ability to pay and never requested the transfer certificate the move required. The deal fell through, and Liège suspended him.

He won five years later, and thousands of players have earned more from his case than he ever did.

The Bosman ruling of December 15, 1995 stopped clubs from demanding a fee for an out-of-contract player moving to a club in another EU member state.

It did not end every form of post-contract compensation worldwide, whatever the legend says.

When it comes to signings, FIFA’s rules set the timing.

Under article 18(3) of the FIFA Regulations on the Status and Transfer of Players (July 2025 edition), a player may sign with a new club once his contract has expired or is due to expire within six months.

The new club must first tell the current club in writing.

The six months count back from the real end date, so the magic month is not always January.

And signing a future contract is not the same as being registered to play.

Registration still depends on the transfer window and domestic rules.

The signing club may pay wages, a signing-on bonus and agent fees, even when no transfer fee goes to the previous club.

Compare the full contract period and separate one-off payments from annual pay before judging which deal costs less.

Illustrative five-year signing costs. Original SoccerNews editorial example using hypothetical figures, not a real transfer or market average.

Calculation: fee-paying = £20m + (5 × £3m) + £1m + £2m = £38m. Out-of-contract = £0 + (5 × £5m) + £5m + £3m = £33m. Annual wages are counted once, through the five-year total. Assumptions: both players complete five full years; wages are fixed gross amounts; bonuses and agent fees are paid by the signing club and counted once. Excludes employer payroll charges, taxes, performance bonuses, financing, add-ons, training compensation, resale income and early termination. These are nominal commitments, not cash schedules or accounting expenses.

In this hypothetical example, the free signing costs £33m over five years, compared with £38m for the fee-paying signing.

Higher wages and signing costs absorb much of the saved fee. Different contract terms could reverse the result.

In other words, the costs shift between transfer fees, wages and other signing expenses.

Which brings us to the most confusing pair of words in football. A free agent is the player. A football agent is the representative who negotiates for him, and sometimes for a club. Only one of those job titles contains the word “free.” Neither of them works for free.

Premier League clubs reported £460.3 million in payments to football agents for the period from February 4, 2025 to February 2, 2026, according to The FA.

The figure covers reported agent payments across different types of transactions, including some agreed before the reporting period. It should not be read as the cost of free transfers alone.

Premier League Squad Cost Ratio (SCR) rules in force for 2026/27 assess defined squad costs against relevant revenue and player-sale results.

The 85% Green Threshold operates alongside additional allowance and a Red Threshold, so crossing 85% does not automatically trigger a points deduction. Free signings still create relevant costs through pay and other deal expenses. (Premier League)

In plain terms, every pound spent on the squad now fights for the same space.

Squad costs include wages, agent fees and transfer fees spread over time, a process called amortization. Since the Premier League’s five-year rule for new or extended contracts, a fee can be spread over five years at most.

So a £20m fee on a five-year deal adds £4m a year to the accounts (£20m ÷ 5). This assumes straight-line accounting and no early sale or write-down. It is an accounting charge, not the cash payment, which can follow a different schedule.

In this example, an out-of-contract signing avoids the £4m annual amortization charge linked to the hypothetical £20m transfer fee. The club must still account for the player’s wages and any other signing or registration costs. That is the part of “free” the unveiling photo never shows.

You can follow how this plays out window by window in our Premier League transfers coverage.

A club that lets a player walk is not always being careless.

It weighs sporting value against the price of a renewal, and the player gets a vote too. For the signing club, “free” generally means no transfer fee to the previous club, not a cost-free deal.

Under FIFA’s July 2025 regulations, a professional may conclude a contract with another club when his current contract has expired or is due to expire within six months. The approaching club must first inform the current club in writing. Domestic rules and the regulatory edition in force must also be checked.

Some out-of-contract players can be registered outside a registration period under specified exceptions. Being unattached does not create an unlimited right to register at any time. The date the contract ended, association rules and competition eligibility all matter.

No transfer fee does not always mean no compensation. Training-compensation rules can apply to qualifying young players, and domestic schemes may also apply. Contract expiry is different from early termination, which can raise other compensation questions.

It is a one-off payment a club makes to a player for agreeing to join. A signing-on bonus may be substantial in a free transfer, but the amount depends on the negotiation.

No. A club can accept an offer, but the player must agree personal terms with the buyer. If he says no, he stays until his contract ends.

Rule summaries are based on the Bosman judgment (C-415/93), the FIFA Regulations on the Status and Transfer of Players (July 2025 edition), Premier League statements on squad-cost rules and amortization, and The FA’s 2025-26 agent-payment report. The cost table is an original SoccerNews example with hypothetical figures. Rules change, so check the edition in force on the date you read this. Browse more football explainers.

#1818. Tottenham seek ban on journalist over anti-Spurs chants with Arsenal fans

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Tottenham have lodged a formal complaint to the Premier League about the actions of a reporter working for ESPN Brasil.

Joao Castelo-Branco, who works as an English football correspondent for ESPN, was seen in video footage shared on his personal social media taking part in anti-Tottenham chanting with Arsenal fans in Sao Paulo.

The video was shared on Castelo-Branco’s personal Instagram page as well as an account belonging to an ESPN podcast and has now led to Spurs filing an official complaint against the journalist.

As part of their complaint, Tottenham have asked the Premier League to prevent Castelo-Branco from covering the club in future. That includes attending matches, press conferences and potential interviews.

The exclusions would not affect any other reporter or the broadcaster themselves, with ESPN a Premier League rights holder in the Caribbean and South America.

Castelo-Branco apologised for his actions in an interview with The Times and said the videos had since been removed from both social media accounts.

“I wanted to apologise to the club for the video I recorded with Arsenal fans in Brazil singing a derogatory chant about Tottenham Hotspur,” Castelo-Branco said. “Given my role as a correspondent in the UK, I feel I made a mistake.

“The video was posted on the podcast Instagram page and reproduced on my personal page. I understand it can be offensive to Spurs and Spurs fans and I should have thought more about singing that and the reach it could have.

“ESPN was notified by the Premier League about Tottenham seeing and disliking the post, and we agreed to delete it. Hopefully we can move on, and I will rethink and be more careful with the boundaries of having that persona on the podcast.”

#1817. Man United: Every Big Six club's worst Premier League finish after Red Devils plunge into relegation zone

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 08 Nov 2026 12:50

Manchester United have struggled for much of the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era, but they appear to have reached a new low in the 2026-27 Premier League campaign.

Although the Red Devils finished 15th in 2024-25 and were struggling again the following season before Ruben Amorim's dismissal, Michael Carrick inspired a second-half revival that saw them finish third, earning him the permanent manager's job.

However, the former England midfielder has endured a difficult start to his first full campaign in charge, with just one win from their opening nine top-flight games and none in their last seven, leaving the 20-time league champions in a precarious position.

Nottingham Forest's 3-1 victory over Manchester City on Saturday had a knock-on effect on the Premier League table, pushing United down to 18th and into the relegation zone ahead of their gameweek 10 clash with Aston Villa later on Sunday, marking their first time in the bottom three nine games into a season since 1986.

Things could get even worse if Crystal Palace avoid defeat at home to Liverpool and Sunderland beat Chelsea, as that combination would leave United bottom of the table before they even take to the pitch at Old Trafford.

With the situation looking increasingly unusual for a club of United's stature, attention turns to the other heavyweights who have found themselves in trouble, and Sports Mole looks at the worst Premier League finish of every traditional top-six side, ranked from worst to best.

City's failure to win the Premier League title in back-to-back seasons in 2024-25 and 2025-26 felt like an anomaly for a club that had claimed six crowns in seven years under Pep Guardiola, but the Citizens have not always enjoyed such lofty standards.

Before Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan's takeover in 2008, City spent much of their time in mid-table and twice finished 18th in the Premier League era, suffering relegation on both occasions.

The first came in 1995-96 under Alan Ball, whose side collected just two points from their opening 11 league games before finishing the campaign with 38 points, having won nine, drawn 11 and lost 18.

The outcome went down to the final day, when City came from 2-0 down against Liverpool at half time to draw 2-2, but they were still relegated on goal difference after Ball, believing a draw would be enough, had his players run down the clock.

The Cityzens’ second relegation came in 2000-01 under Joe Royle, following back-to-back promotions, with a 4-0 opening-day defeat to Charlton Athletic setting the tone for a difficult campaign and marquee signing George Weah leaving in October after just 11 appearances.

Relegation was confirmed with defeat at Ipswich Town, leading to Royle's dismissal, before Kevin Keegan took charge and guided City straight back up as Division One champions, although it remained their third relegation in six years, a period that had also seen them drop into the third tier in 1998.

Tottenham's worst Premier League finish has now come in successive seasons, with Spurs ending both 2024-25 and 2025-26 in 17th place.

In 2024-25, Ange Postecoglou's injury-hit side lost 22 of their 38 league games, becoming the first top-flight team to suffer that many defeats and still avoid relegation, finishing on 38 points.

Remarkably, the campaign still ended with the club lifting their first European trophy in 41 years, courtesy of a 1-0 victory over Manchester United in the Europa League final in Bilbao, although Postecoglou was sacked just 16 days later.

The following season brought even more turmoil, as Thomas Frank was dismissed in February 2026 after an eight-game winless run left Spurs 16th, before Igor Tudor lasted just 44 days prior to his own departure.

Roberto De Zerbi was then handed a long-term contract with relegation looming, and victories over Wolverhampton Wanderers and Aston Villa gave Spurs renewed hope heading into the final day.

A 1-0 home win over Everton took them to 41 points and kept them in 17th place, sending West Ham United down on 39 points despite their 3-0 victory over Leeds United.

United's lowest Premier League finish came just two seasons ago, when they ended the 2024-25 campaign in 15th place with 42 points and 44 goals scored, both representing club lows.

Erik ten Hag was sacked in October 2024 after just nine league games, only months after signing a contract extension, with Ruud van Nistelrooy taking temporary charge before Amorim inherited a side sitting 12th in the table.

Matters deteriorated further under the Portuguese coach, who admitted in January 2025 that his team might be the worst in the club's history, with United suffering 18 league defeats that season, their highest tally since being relegated in 1973-74.

The Red Devils also failed to win consecutive league games throughout the campaign for the first time in the club's history before ending the season with defeat to Spurs in the Europa League final, leaving them without European football the following term.

United bounced back to finish third under Carrick in 2025-26, but their return to the bottom three just nine games into the current campaign has made that 15th-placed finish look rather less like a low point.

Chelsea's worst Premier League finish came in 1993-94, when they ended the 42-game season in 14th place with 51 points from 13 wins, 12 draws and 17 defeats.

Glenn Hoddle's arrival as player-manager had raised hopes after previous bosses had struggled to take the club beyond mid-table, but the league campaign never really gathered momentum.

The season included an 11-game winless run, while a 4-1 defeat at Leeds United proved their heaviest loss of the campaign.

There was some consolation in the cups, with Gavin Peacock scoring twice in the semi-final victory over Luton Town to send Chelsea into their first FA Cup final in 24 years.

Man United ran out 4-0 winners in the final, with Eric Cantona scoring twice, but their status as league champions meant they were heading for the Champions League, leaving Chelsea to take the Cup Winners' Cup place as runners-up.

The campaign proved to be the beginning of a rebuild that would eventually bring Ruud Gullit to Stamford Bridge.

Arsenal entered the 1994-95 campaign as a club accustomed to winning trophies, having claimed the league title in 1991, both domestic cups in 1993 and the Cup Winners' Cup in 1994, yet they finished 12th, their lowest league placing since 1976.

The season began poorly, with the Gunners scoring in just one of their opening five league games, and they never managed to escape mid-table, eventually finishing on 51 points in a 42-game campaign, just six clear of the relegation zone.

George Graham was sacked on February 21, 1995, after it emerged that he had accepted a £425,000 payment from agent Rune Hauge, and he was subsequently banned from football for a year by the FA.

Assistant Stewart Houston stepped in and won his first two games, but his arrival coincided with a run of six defeats in seven matches that left Arsenal in real danger of relegation.

The threat was greater than usual because four clubs were going down that season as the Premier League prepared to reduce from 22 teams to 20.

Arsenal at least had Ian Wright's 18 league goals and a run to the Cup Winners' Cup final to take some encouragement from, but Nayim's remarkable lob from more than 40 yards over David Seaman in the closing seconds of extra time handed Real Zaragoza the trophy.

Liverpool are the only traditional top-six side never to have finished below eighth in the Premier League era, although they have ended the campaign in that position on three occasions.

The first came in 1993-94, when Graeme Souness resigned in January following a home FA Cup defeat to Bristol City, leaving bootroom stalwart Roy Evans to take charge.

That campaign marked Robbie Fowler's breakthrough season and the final year of the Kop as a standing terrace, but it also saw Liverpool suffer 16 league defeats, their highest tally in a Premier League season.

In 2011-12, Kenny Dalglish's side collected 52 points, their lowest total since 1954, in a campaign overshadowed by Luis Suarez's eight-match ban for racially abusing Patrice Evra and lengthy injury absences for Lucas Leiva and Steven Gerrard.

The Merseyside Reds did lift the League Cup, beating Cardiff City on penalties to end a six-year trophy drought, but won only four of their next 11 league games and lost the FA Cup final to Chelsea, a run of results that ultimately cost Dalglish his job.

The third eighth-placed finish came in 2015-16, when Brendan Rodgers was sacked in October with Liverpool sitting 10th, before Jurgen Klopp took over four days later and guided the Reds to two finals, only to lose both against Man City on penalties and Sevilla.

#1814. Atletico Madrid willing to wait for Alvarez to hit form

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Diego Simeone is willing to be patient with Julian Alvarez, who he feels is vital to getting Atletico Madrid to where they want to be.

Alvarez has netted just twice in all competitions this season, while providing three assists.

His latest goal involvement came on Sunday, as he teed up Giuliano Simeone to open the scoring against Barcelona. The Blaugrana, though, went on to win 2-1.

Barca pushed hard to sign Alvarez this past summer, with Atletico refusing to budge and even threatening legal action against the reigning LaLiga champions.

And though Alvarez is yet to hit his peak form, Simeone is willing to wait.

"He's an extraordinary player, we love him dearly, we need him, we need the best Julian, and we're going to work with him," the Atletico boss told Movistar+.

"Of the team's five good scoring opportunities, he was involved in three or four. He just lacked the goal that would have made him stand out, but it will come."

In his post-match press conference, Simeone added of Alvarez: "We all wish he had scored, but we'll wait for him; we need him because if we want to get where we want to go, we need him, otherwise we won't get there."

Asked if Alvarez was suffering from a lack of confidence, Simeone replied: "I'm not in his body, he has our trust."

— Atlético de Madrid (@atletienglish) November 9, 2026

Alvarez led Atletico for shots (four), touches in the opposition box (seven) and successful dribbles (three), while also creating two chances.

Atletico's defeat snapped a seven-game winning run in LaLiga. They sit third, two points behind second-place Real Madrid and five adrift of leaders Barca.

"I'm left with an outstanding performance from the players, nothing to complain about," Simeone told reporters.

"We put the opposing players in a position where they weren't comfortable. We lacked the clinical finishing we've shown on other occasions, and they're a very confident opponent who capitalised on their chances.

"I'm proud of the lads, I loved it, and I'm very happy with everyone's performance."

Burton Albion will be looking to secure their place in the EFL Trophy knockout stages when they welcome Notts County to the Pirelli Stadium on Tuesday.

The visitors have already qualified, but Burton still have work to do if they are to join them.

Burton currently sit 15th in League One with 17 points from 14 matches, but they have only won one of their last six league matches.

The Brewers suffered a 2-0 defeat away to Wycombe Wanderers in their most recent league outing, but they responded positively on Saturday by recording a convincing 4-0 win over Rushden and Diamonds in the FA Cup.

Will Collar, Raphael Borges Rodrigues, Charlie Webster and Zac Scutt all scored for Gary Bowyer's side and they will be looking to carry that momentum into Tuesday's game.

Burton have collected three points from their opening two EFL Trophy matches, losing to Nottingham Forest Under-21s on penalties after a 1-1 draw and then beating Grimsby Town on penalties after a 0-0 draw.

A victory over Notts County on Tuesday would guarantee Burton a place in the knockout stages.

Notts County, meanwhile, sit 17th in League One with 14 points from 12 matches and are just three points behind Burton with a game in hand.

Martin Paterson's side head into Tuesday's clash after a dramatic FA Cup encounter against Altrincham on Saturday, which saw them draw 2-2 before winning on penalties.

Jacob Bedeau gave Notts County an early lead, but Altrincham fought back with goals from Lucas Weaver and Lewis Banks before Callum Roberts netted a late equaliser.

Although they have already guaranteed qualification for the next round, the visitors will be keen to continue their good form as they are currently unbeaten in their last four games across all competitions.

Burton could reward Scutt with a start after he came off the bench to score against Rushden and Diamonds, with the 18-year-old set to feature in attack alongside Charlie Webster and Mark O'Mahony.

Collar and Kegs Chauke are set to continue in midfield, with Borges Rodrigues and Emeka Adiele likely to feature out wide.

Notts County will be hoping Roberts can continue his good form, having scored in their last two games.

Daniel Kanu and Luka Smyth are set to lead the line ahead of Roberts, while Nick Tsaroulla and Ishe Samuels-Smith are expected to start out wide.

Published: 03:13 EST, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 06:06 EST, 5 November 2026

Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane has extended his contract at Bayern Munich until 2029 in a move that will make him Europe's highest-paid player.

According to reports in Germany, his bumper new deal takes his weekly wages to a staggering £400,000 - believed to be the highest base salary in the continent.

Kane scored 73 goals in 65 appearances for club and country last season, earning him the award for the world's best player ahead of Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal at last week's ceremony in London.

Tthe England captain has scored 156 goals in 161 games since joining Bayern from Tottenham Hotspur in 2023.

Kane was entering the final six months of his deal at Bayern but any hope of returning to the Premier League to break Alan Shearer's goalscoring record has been dashed, as he commits another three years to the German champions.

The 33-year-old has settled into life in Bavaria with ease, moving to Germany with his wife and childhood sweetheart, Kate, and their four children to embark on a new life together three years ago.

Signing his new deal, Kane said: 'I feel right at home at FC Bayern. I love the club, the fans and the city of Munich.

Harry Kane's new deal will extend his stay in Germany to at least 2029

Kane has scored 156 goals at almost one a game since joining from Tottenham in 2023

'We have a fantastic team and, in Vincent Kompany, a fantastic manager. It makes me very proud to be part of this club.

'My whole family is very happy here. I was keen to stay. I'm now looking forward to the future and I want to win many more titles with this great club.'

Kane had never lifted silverware before joining Bayern but has made up for it in the last two years, claiming two Bundesliga titles, the DFB Cup and two German Super Cups.

He has earned plenty of individual honours, too. Alongside the Ballon d'Or, Kane has been Bundesliga top goalscorer in both seasons and has twice won the Golden Shoe, which recognises Europe's best striker. He was also crowned Germany's best player last season.

For country, Kane led England to their best World Cup finish since 1966 this summer, as the Three Lions won bronze. Kane scored six goals in seven outings for Thomas Tuchel's side.

Later this month, Kane is poised to become England's record appearance holder when the Three Lions face Croatia and Spain in the Nations League. He currently shares the record with Peter Shilton, with the pair capped 125 times.

Kane and his family have settled into life in Germany with ease. Pictured with wife, Kate

Kane is already England's all-time leading goalscorer, having netted 91 times - 38 more than second-placed Wayne Rooney.

He told The Guardian in 2024: '[The children are] in school now and have been skiing the last couple of weekends. Just having that has been great for them. We've met a few of the parents at school and made friends with teammates' wives and kids.

'Slowly but surely it starts to feel like home. People ask what are the big differences, but a lot of the routine is pretty much the same.

'You miss friends you have at home or a golf course, but you soon learn about those things here and it becomes part of your home.

'They’re loving it. They’ll be speaking the language before me too.'

#1809. Sunderland suffer Granit Xhaka injury blow against Chelsea as Regis Le Bris forced into early change

By Ben Knapton | 08 Nov 2026 14:17, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 14:37

Sunderland were dealt a major injury concern just a few minutes into their Premier League clash with Chelsea, as Granit Xhaka was forced off with a suspected calf problem.

The former Arsenal man unsurprisingly started the Stadium of Light encounter against the Blues, who were interested in signing him during the summer transfer window.

Xhaka ultimately snubbed interest from the West London giants to remain with Sunderland, but he did not get the chance to show his former admirers what they are missing out on.

With just a couple of minutes gone on Sunday afternoon, the Switzerland international dropped to the turf and eventually had to hobble off after receiving treatment.

Xhaka - who was replaced by Jules Ahoka - appeared to have sustained a calf problem, although he was able to take his place on the bench shortly after being withdrawn.

Regis Le Bris will be quizzed for an update on Xhaka's injury at full time, but Sunderland will need to send the midfielder for tests to determine the severity of his problem.

However, if Xhaka has suffered a calf injury as expected, the 34-year-old's recuperation period could range from a couple of weeks to a few months depending on the grade of his concern.

A Grade 1 issue - or mild strain - usually takes one to two weeks to heal, meaning that Xhaka could return in time for Sunderland's clash with Aston Villa on November 21 following the international break.

A Grade 2 injury could rule Xhaka out for up to six weeks, though, putting him at risk of missing games against Jagiellonia Bialystok, Tottenham Hotspur, Liverpool, Newcastle United, AC Milan, Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace between now and Christmas.

Meanwhile, a Grade 3 injury - a complete tear - would likely sideline Xhaka for three months, forcing him to sit out clashes with Manchester United, Chelsea and Liverpool either side of the New Year.

Xhaka was making his 14th appearance of the season for Sunderland in all competitions before being withdrawn, and he played the full 90 minutes in each of the Black Cats' first nine Premier League matches of the campaign.

Le Bris is already without fellow midfielder Habib Diarra due to a thigh injury, and the 22-year-old is not anticipated to return before the middle of December.

With Diarra on the sidelines, Ahoka is the most natural alternative to Xhaka alongside Noah Sadiki, although Le Bris could also consider a couple of emergency options amid the hectic schedule.

Enzo Le Fee could start in a deeper position, as could Chris Rigg, although Sunderland are already lighter in attack with Romaine Mundle (knee) out until 2027.

Alternatively, Le Bris could bring 31-year-old midfielder Alan Browne back into the fold; the Irishman spent last season on loan at Middlesbrough and has been restricted to just two EFL Cup appearances for Sunderland so far this season.

#1808. Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Home » Home 2 » Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Table-toppers Arsenal travel to Anfield tonight with their first Premier League trophy since the ‘invincibles’ season of 2004 in sight. The Gunners top the table and with stuttering performances from Manchester City and a Leicester City whose fairytale run seems at an end, and are in pole position to finish the current campaign as champions.

While Jurgen Klopp’s men are still finding their way inconsistently since his appointment, Arsenal are in top form with five victories out of their last six matches. In comparison, Liverpool have been as easy to predict as a magic 8 ball, with impressive wins over Leicester City and Manchester City, but accompanied with horrific losses against Watford and West Ham. With fourth place still within grasp and with an impressive record against the table topping teams this season, Liverpool would look to give their long suffering fans some cheer with which to greet this New Year.

The Reds desperately need a victory to steady the ship as their erratic and wayward form sees them enter 2016 still outside the top 4 and distant from any title challenge.

With a host of injuries to his main XI, Jurgen Klopp could be forgiven for dipping into the transfer market so early. The Reds have captured QPR right-back Steven Caulker along with Marko Grujic in the January transfer window.

With Grujic returning to his former club Red Star Belgrade on loan, Steven Caulker is likely to be given a run out as a substitute with the current spate of Liverpool injuries.

Ings, Sturridge, Lovren, Coutinho, Origi and Flanagan are amongst the Liverpool afflicted and will take no part in the match ahead. With Lovren out, Kolo Toure and Mamadou Sakho look likely to be Klopp’s first choice central defending partnership.

Alberto Moreno and Nathaniel Clyne should start as full-backs for the Liverpool side and will be crucial in any attempt to penetrate the Gunner’s defences. Emre Can and Lucas should marshal the midfield, while James Milner, Firmino and Adam Lallana look to give Petr Cech some concerns about his goal. Leading the line should be Christian Benteke, who’s lack of form doesn’t threaten this match as manager Klopp has few options in his position.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Mignolet; Clyne, Sakho, Toure, Moreno; Lucas, Can, Firmino, Lallana, Milner, Benteke.

Arsenal must show that they have the one quality required of all champions : Consistency. The task is hereby straightforward for Wenger’s men. Win, keep winning, regardless of your manner and the title is yours.

With half the season concluded, Arsene Wenger must be wishing that he received a Christmas gift from the Arsenal medical team. Injuries have decimated his midfield with Wilshire, Cazorla, Rosiscky, Coquelin and Sanchez out of the game.

There is some good news with Mesul Ozil having managed to partake in some leisure instead of participating in the FA cup victory over Sunderland. Keeping the nimble playmaker fit would be key to Arsenal aspirations, both in this match and for the remainder of the season.

With both Petr Mertersacker and Gabriel available, it would be interesting to see whom Arsene Wenger picks out for his starting XI. Koscielny, Bellerin and Monreal have nailed down their place in the defence and the inclusion of the slower Mertersacker or the inconsistent Gabriel may have a defining moment in the game.

With Arsenal’s midfield woes, it should fall to Flamini to screen the defence with Ramsey alongside him. Walcott, Ozil and Joel Campbell should be the main thrusts of Arsenal’s attacking play with Giroud as the elegant, decisive focus.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Cech; Bellerin, Gabriel, Koscielny, Monreal; Flamini, Ramsey, Ozil, Walcott, Campbell; Girourd.

With previous encounters between these teams resulting in high scoring draws, we favour a repeat of last year’s epic 2-2 result for the same fixture. Martin Skrtel’s 97th minute header in front of the Kop capped a memorable game which also had Fabio Borini sent off and we expect similar fireworks at Anfield tomorrow.

#1806. Man United, Arsenal handed huge early suspension boosts after Igor Thiago VAR decision

By Ben Knapton | 08 Nov 2026 14:46, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 15:02

Manchester United and Arsenal have been handed huge early boosts for their Premier League clashes with Brentford, which Igor Thiago will miss through suspension.

The Brazil international started up top for the Bees in their trip to Brighton & Hove Albion, but things quickly unravelled for Keith Andrews's side at the Amex Stadium.

Brentford fell 1-0 down within 15 minutes to a Diego Gomez goal, before Thiago and Chema Andres were involved in a set-to, which saw Thiago shove the Brighton man in the face.

The striker was initially booked for his role in the incident, but upon reviewing the incident on the pitchside monitor, referee Michael Oliver issued a straight red card to Thiago.

"After review, Brentford No.9 pushes his opponent in the face with force. Yellow card is cancelled and the final decision is red card," Oliver announced to the crowd, as Thiago prepares to serve a three-game suspension.

Brentford are a goal down and now a man down ? Igor Thiago is sent off after a VAR review. Referee Michael Oliver says he pushed Brighton's Chema Andres "in the face with force." https://t.co/YMZrYFUGyx

As the Brentford man was dismissed for violent conduct, he will be forced to sit out the Bees' next three matches against Everton, Man United and Arsenal after the international break.

Thiago begins his ban against Everton on November 23, before Andrews's men travel to Man United on November 28, and he completes his suspension against champions Arsenal on December 2.

The 25-year-old's punishment could be revoked if Brentford are successful with an appeal, but it is extremely unlikely that the Bees would win their case if they decided to contest the decision.

Andrews will therefore have to cope without his chief centre-forward for crunch clashes with Arsenal and Man Utd, although Thiago has so far struggled to replicate his 22-goal form from 2025-26.

The South American has scored just two goals and set up two more in 10 Premier League games this season, although each one of those contributions came in his last five full appearances.

Thiago's absence is especially untimely for Brentford, as Andrews is also working without another striker - 19-year-old Kaye Furo - due to a serious foot injury.

Furo has made "really good progress" in his recuperation, though, and there is a chance that the 2007-born striker could be ready for competitive action following the international break.

However, Thiago's ban could instead open the door for 34-year-old veteran Callum Wilson to make his first Premier League starts of the season, as the Englishman has made just six substitute appearances in the 2026-27 English top flight so far.

Dango Ouattara and Kevin Schade could also be deployed as auxiliary centre-forwards, but Thiago's absence nevertheless represents a major blow for Brentford, and a major boost for Arsenal and Man Utd.

#1804. Prediction: Ivory Coast vs Gambia

Ivory Coast and Gambia will meet at Stade de la Paix in Bouake on Thursday, November 12, as the two early leaders in Group C continue their qualification campaigns for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations.

Both teams have collected six points from their opening two matches. Ivory Coast has done so without conceding, while Gambia arrives after scoring six goals against Somalia and Ghana.

Verdict: Over 2.5 goals Best odds: 16/25 Bookmaker: 1xBet

Ivory Coast has made a convincing start to qualifying, beating Ghana and Somalia by the same 2-0 scoreline. Those results have put the Elephants in a strong position before a pair of matches against their closest challenger.

Gambia has already won away to Ghana and has enough attacking quality to cause problems if the home side commits too many players forward.

Still, Ivory Coast has several ways to stretch the visiting defense. Amad Diallo, Nicolas Pepe and Yan Diomande give Renard options out wide, where beating the first defender could force Gambia’s central players out of position.

That should be an important part of the home side’s approach. Moving the ball quickly between the wings would make it harder for Gambia to protect the middle and give Ivory Coast opportunities to deliver into the penalty area.

The Elephants won the most recent meeting 1-0 in March 2025. Their opening qualifying results also suggest they can manage a game without allowing much at the other end.

However, Gambia’s attacking form gives this meeting a different feel. Ivory Coast may need to keep looking for goals even after taking the lead.

Renard has confirmed that Amad Diallo is fit following the injury concern that forced him off during his club’s match on October 31.

Odilon Kossounou and Guela Doue are absent from the squad. Evan Ndicka, Ousmane Diomande and Emmanuel Agbadou remain available in central defense, while Oumar Solet is among the new additions to the group.

Franck Kessie and Ibrahim Sangare offer experience in midfield, with Malick Yalcouye another option.

Further forward, Renard can choose from Amad, Pepe, Yan Diomande, Bazoumana Toure and Martial Godo, alongside central attacking options Elye Wahi and Bonny.

There is enough variety to change the attack during the match, particularly if Gambia manages to close the spaces around its penalty area.

Gambia’s opening results deserve attention. The Scorpions began with a 2-1 victory over Somalia before producing a 4-2 comeback win away to Ghana.

That second performance showed how dangerous this team can be when a match opens up. Gambia trailed 2-0 in Accra before Mohamed Badamosi and Omar Colley brought it level before halftime. Ebrima Colley then scored twice after the break to complete the turnaround.

Recovering from that position should give Johnathan McKinstry’s players confidence heading into another difficult away assignment. They have already shown that falling behind does not have to end their chances.

The defensive side of those performances is worth considering, though. Gambia conceded against Somalia and allowed Ghana to establish a two-goal lead. Similar lapses in Bouake could prove expensive.

McKinstry will probably want his midfield to stay close to the defense while leaving enough support for counterattacks. Sitting too deep for long periods would invite repeated pressure from Ivory Coast’s wide players.

There should be opportunities to break when the hosts push forward. Whether Gambia can use those moments effectively may determine how competitive this match becomes.

Gambia has been boosted by the return of Musa Barrow and Yankuba Minteh, who missed the opening two qualifiers through injury.

Their availability gives McKinstry additional attacking options alongside Ebrima Colley and Badamosi, both of whom contributed to the successful start.

However, Jesper Ceesay and Suleiman Camara have subsequently withdrawn because of injuries. Saidou Khan and Salieu Drammeh have been called up as their replacements.

Alieu Fadera is also unavailable with a thigh injury. Omar Colley offers experience in defense, while Ebou Adams and Abubakarr Barry are among the midfield options.

The returning attackers should help Gambia carry a threat beyond its own half. McKinstry will need that outlet if his team spends long stretches defending.

Ivory Coast should create enough chances to put Gambia’s defense under sustained pressure. The visitors have conceded in both qualifiers, and recovering from another poor start would be difficult against this opposition.

Gambia also has reasons to believe it can contribute to the scoring. Six goals in two qualifiers, followed by the return of Barrow and Minteh, give the away side a credible attacking threat.

Another controlled 2-0 home win is the main concern for this selection. Even so, the attacking options available and Gambia’s defensive vulnerabilities make over 2.5 goals the preferred bet.

Verdict: Over 2.5 goals Best odds: 16/25 Bookmaker: 1xBet

#1803. Ipswich vs. Bournemouth: Evanilson makes history after shocking goalkeeper error

By Ben Knapton | 08 Nov 2026 15:12, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 15:26

Evanilson etched his name into the Bournemouth history books by opening the scoring in Sunday's Premier League clash with Ipswich Town.

The Brazil international came into the Portman Road battle in hot goalscoring form, having netted in four top-flight games in succession.

However, Evanilson was gifted one of the easiest goals he will ever score in English football against Ipswich, thanks to a shocking mistake from Tractor Boys goalkeeper Christian Walton.

Under pressure from Evanilson, Walton attempted to drag the ball away from the Bournemouth striker rather than clearing his lines, but he was robbed of possession by the South American.

Evanilson evaded Walton's desperate sprawling grasp and slotted the ball into an empty net, thus becoming the first Bournemouth player in history to score in five straight Premier League games.

It's Evanilson again for Bournemouth! ? A nightmare for Christian Walton and Evanilson makes no mistake https://t.co/QYGU9Xaniv

The 27-year-old's scoring sequence began on October 10, when he netted the Cherries' consolation goal in their 5-1 hammering at the hands of Chelsea at Stamford Bridge.

Evanilson then found the net in each of his three remaining Premier League games in October, helping to propel Bournemouth to victory against Sunderland, Manchester United and Leeds United.

The Brazilian failed to score in any of his first five league appearances of the campaign, but he has now moved onto nine direct involvements from his first 10 games, having also chalked up four assists.

Evanilson has also registered three goal contributions from four Europa League games - two of his own and one assist - while managing 12 in total across 14 outings in all tournaments.

Following the South American's early opener, Bournemouth doubled their lead on the stroke of half time through a Leif Davis own goal, putting Marco Rose's men on the verge of a fourth successive Premier League victory.

By making the net bulge at Portman Road, Evanilson moved above Junior Stanislas into outright seventh place in Bournemouth's all-time Premier League scoring charts.

The Brazilian is now just one behind teammate Justin Kluivert and two adrift of Marcus Tavernier, who is the highest active scorer in the Cherries' squad with 23 to his name.

Dominic Solanke's 28 and Antoine Semenyo's 30 are also within reach for Evanilson this season, but the Brazilian may need to wait a while longer to surpass Callum Wilson's 41 or Josh King's unparalleled 48.

Eli Junior Kroupi is further down the list in 10th place, but the much-coveted Frenchman boasts the best goals-per-game ratio of any Bournemouth Premier League player with 0.37.

#1802. AC Milan Women 0-3 Inter: Chances squandered and a silly red card

Milan Women failed to replicate the heroics of the men’s team in the Derby della Madonnina, conceding three goals against Inter after a silly red card.

After the odd-goal defeat to Como last night time out, Milan Women were out for revenge this afternoon, and perhaps also a little inspired by the men’s win in the derby last weekend. However, Suzanne Bakker’s side made life very difficult for themselves.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In the first half, Milan actually had a couple of good opportunities to take the lead and make it a very different game. After just four minutes, the veteran Christy Grimshaw got a good chance in the box, but failed to connect with the cross from the left with her head from close range.

About ten minutes later, Mawa Sesay picked up on a loose ball after a mistake by Inter’s backline. However, she somehow missed the target and didn’t even force the goalkeeper to a save, effectively squandering a 1v1 by rushing the shot.

In the second half, the game remained fairly even but one moment proved costly for Milan. As Benedetta Glionna made her way into the box, the aforementioned Grimshaw made her evening worse with a little kick, resulting in a penalty for the away side (somewhat cheap, but fair).

Haley Bugeja made no mistakes from the spot, firing a great shot straight down the middle to give her side the lead in the 57th minute. Milan then began their pursuit of an equaliser after that but instead of a goal, around five minutes later, Sandra Ogalla was sent off.

The goalkeeper used her hands a little bit too early, touching the ball outside the penalty box, and the referee immediately spotted it. Bakker made use of the VAR challenge, prompting the referee to have a look at the screen, but the decision was upheld. A silly red card indeed.

Deputy goalkeeper Sally Rainey was brought on but just a few minutes later, Inter doubled their lead through Glionna. It was a well-worked move, in fairness, but the defending could have been better at the far post. That was in the 67th minute.

Milan tried to get back into the game but struggled with only ten players. And so, in the 83rd minute, Inter were awarded another penalty. This one was even cheaper than the first, as Angelica Soffia barely touched the player.

Despite another VAR check, the decision was upheld and Bugeja bagged her second of the night. That concluded the night from a goalscoring point of view, and Milan Women suffered their second consecutive defeat.

#1801. FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

Home » Home 2 » FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

The ban will start from the July transfer window this year and finish with the January transfer market in 2017.

Atletico were also fined 900,000 Swiss francs (820,000 euros) and Real 360,000 (330,000 euros).

“The two clubs were found to have violated several provisions concerning the international transfer and first registration of minor players as well as other relevant provisions with regard to the registration and participation of certain players in competitions,” said a FIFA statement.

Barcelona has just ended a one year ban for similar reasons.

Real and Atletico were “issued with a reprimand and given 90 days in which to regularise the situation of all minor players concerned,” FIFA said. They can still sell players during the transfer ban.

FIFA said the alarm was raised over the two clubs by FIFA’s Transfer Matching System and its disciplinary committee completed the inquiry.

Under international football rules, players under 18 cannot be transferred to another country, except in limited circumstances. All transfers need the approval of a special FIFA committee.

“The investigations concerned minor players who were involved and participated in competitions with the clubs over various periods between 2007 and 2014 (Atletico Madrid) and between 2005 and 2014 (Real Madrid),” FIFA said.

The ban follows a similar sanction handed to European champions Barcelona, who were unable to register new players during 2015.

Barca were initially banned in April 2014, but managed to delay the sanction taking affect until the transfer windows in January and the summer 2015 by launching an ultimately unsuccessful appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

By delaying the ban, Barca managed to sign the likes of Luis Suarez and Ivan Rakitic in the summer of 2014 to propel them to a treble of La Liga, Champions League and Copa del Rey.

The news is just the latest institutional embarassment for Real Madrid just over a week after they appointed French legend Zinedine Zidane.

Madrid have sacked two Champions League winning coaches in Carlo Ancelotti and Rafael Benitez in the past seven months, as well as being thrown out of the Copa del Rey for fielding an ineligible player.

The sanction could also be bad news for the likes of Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester United, who had targeted Madrid stars Cristiano Ronaldo and Gareth Bale with Real highly unlikely to dispose of their best players without the chance to sign suitable replacements.

La Liga leaders Atletico Madrid’s usually hectic transfer policy will also be put on hold. However, Diego Simeone’s men look better placed to cope with the ban having invested heavily in young talent over the past year.

Neither Real no Atletico made an immediate comment on whether they would appeal.

#1800. Man United co-owner Avram Glazer 'says they don't NEED success on the pitch to make money' - just like the New York Yankees and Dallas Cowboys

Published: 06:18 EST, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 06:48 EST, 5 November 2026

Manchester United co-owner Avram Glazer has claimed the club’s value is not dependent on success on the pitch.

The figurehead of the hugely unpopular Glazer family addressed an audience at Deutsche Bank’s inaugural Sports Investment Conference in London.

The topic of United’s underperformance on the pitch and whether there is a clear link between on-pitch performance and commercial success came up from an audience member and Glazer was robust in response.

According to the Athletic, the United co-chairman is said to have likened the club to major sporting franchises and brands such as the Dallas Cowboys and the New York Yankees, two teams that haven’t won the Super Bowl or the World Series for years. The Cowboys were last victorious in 1996, and the Yankees in 2009.

United, who haven’t won a Premier League title since 2013 when Sir Alex Ferguson departed, have a rich history as one of the biggest teams in the world but have fallen on hard times in recent years on the pitch, leading to major protests against the Glazer ownership.

United are 17th in the Premier League heading into Sunday’s home game against Aston Villa, hovering precariously above the relegation zone. Any relegation, however unlikely, would be financially devastating.

According to the Glazers, Manchester United's value is not dependent on success on the pitch

It's no wonder Red Devils fans have lost faith in the Glazer family's ownership of their club

But Glazer, who was speaking at the event in September but whose remarks have only just come to light, remains bullish that United are shielded from much fluctuation in their commercial revenue due to the scale of the club's brand around the world.

United’s commercial revenue has continued to rise, even in the lean post-Ferguson years.

In 2012-13, commercial revenue stood at £152m, and by 2017-18 it was £276m. The 2025-26 figure reported was £317m.

While the United brand remains incredibly strong due to its support around the world and the club’s rich history, performance has knocked them down in terms of financial superiority.

Forbes, a go-to list used by the Glazers, ranked United as the third most valuable club in May of this year, behind Real Madrid and Barcelona. A year prior, only Real Madrid were ahead of them.

For context, United were top of the pile as recently as 2018 and owned that spot for a five-year stretch between 2007 and 2012.

Debt is at the centre of United supporters’ frustration with the Glazers, who leveraged money from banks to take over the club in 2005, with the total debt coming in at £689million as recently as June. That’s a steep increase on the previous year of £52m and it shows no sign of going away.

Ineos have been brought in as a minority owner and while Sir Jim Ratcliffe and his team dictate football decisions, and have done since February 2024, Avram and Joel Glazer remain at the centre of budgets and other key decisions.

Bruno Fernandes celebrates as United stop the rot with a superb comeback win against Roma

Comments made by Glazer in September at this convention for financiers only reinforce what many supporters believe and that’s that the Glazer family are not interested in sporting success and instead only focus on the balance sheet.

Ahead of Tuesday night’s win over Roma in the Champions League, 2,000 green and gold balloons – the colours synonymous with the fans’ protests against the Glazer ownership – filled the Stretford End and tennis balls were later thrown towards the pitch.

In recent weeks, with results and performances on the slide after a summer transfer window that left Michael Carrick short compared to rivals, fans have started to escalate chants against the Glazers, director of football Jason Wilcox and Ineos, calling for them to ‘sell United and f*** off home’.

A rousing rendition of ‘stand up if you hate Glazers’ also whipped Old Trafford into a frenzy before United’s players pulled an unlikely win out of the hat on the pitch to keep hopes of progressing in the Champions League alive.

The other side of this is that Glazer may well have been trying to be bullish in the face of finance folk and investors given the rather bleak debt picture.

That won’t be how it’s viewed in Manchester, though, and it does little to give fans hope that the majority owner and minority owner are both seemingly taking this club in the wrong direction.

However, the two-time Premier League champion is out of contract at the end of this season, and was of interest to Juventus this past summer.

But the Brazilian wants to stay at Liverpool.

"Yes, in my mind," Alisson said when asked if he wants to stay at the club.

"I'm focused on playing every game but in my mind, I'm happy to stay. You know, that depends on a lot of aspects and different situations.

"But my will is to stay. I'm happy here, my family is happy here. I'm still hungry for titles and to deliver good performances.

"I still want to play at the top level for as long as I can. So that's my thinking on that."

When asked about Liverpool's start under Andoni Iraola, Alisson added: "I think you have to manage all the situations.

However, getting the three points might not be the easiest task as Genoa have been in red-hot form lately, and will certainly use all of the support from their fans at the Marassi tomorrow.

➤ Manager: Daniele De Rossi ➤ Form (all comps): W-L-W-W-W (most recent) ➤ Top scorer (Serie A): Osmajic – 4 ➤ Most assists (Serie A): Colombo and El Shaarawy – 2 ➤ Injuries & suspensions: None.

After what was a disastrous start to the 2025-26 season under Patrick Vieira, sitting rock bottom between the 7th and 9th matchdays, Daniele De Rossi was appointed. He quickly brought them above the relegation zone and managed to keep them there, finishing seven points clear in the end.

It was only right to confirm him for this season, as such, and there have been no regrets so far. The start was admittedly dodgy, with one draw and four defeats in the first five games, but there have been four wins and one defeat in the five games since. Crisis very much averted.

The only defeat in the last five games came against De Rossi’s former club as well, namely Roma, who have been on fire at the start of this season. There can be no accusations of the former midfielder throwing the game to benefit his former club, let’s put it that way.

On the flip side, the Rossoblu did keep hold of most of the key players from last season, such as Johan Vasquez, Leo Ostigard, Morten Frendrup, and Lorenzo Colombo. The latter was bought permanently from Milan after a season-long loan, as the conditions for the obligation were triggered.

Some interesting signings were also made, from the veteran (and former Milan man) Stephan El Shaarawy to the familiar face Hamed Traore, who played for Sassuolo between 2019 and 2013. After spells at Bournemouth, Napoli, Auxerre and Marseille, he’s now looking to regain stability.

As for the latest team news, De Rossi has a much better situation than Amorim with no injuries or suspensions to note. Lorenzo Venturino and Elias Havel were both on the sidelines but have returned for this one.

It looks like the former Milan men El Shaarawy and Colombo will start, while Junior Messias could perhaps be introduced from the bench. De Rossi didn’t give much away during his presser in terms of the team selection, but did make sure to express his respect for the Rossoneri.

Dries Mertens celebrating with his team-mates on the touchline after his decisive goal in the 4-2 victory at Sampdoria is typical of the spirit and togetherness that has seen Napoli storm to the top of the Serie A title. It was in dedication to Chelsea loanee Nathaniel Chabolah who recently lost his mother a a nice touch to show that there is much more to life than football, even though they have put themselves in a wonderful position to end Juventusa dominance and end a 26-year wait for the Scudetto.

Five straight wins have put Maurizio Sarria s team two points clear at the top, with the former Empoli manager breathing a new lease of life throughout a team that have always looked capable of competing for the title, yet ultimately fallen short when the pressure to deliver grew. He has transformed the entire dynamics of how Napoli play, with clinical attacking movement combined with a rock-solid defence within a 4-3-3 system that is getting the very best from the players at his disposal. This seasona s statistics proved that point; Napoli are far and away the highest scorers in Serie A this season, while only Inter Milan and Juventus have a better defensive record. Just one defeat in the twenty league games since the opening day loss at Sassuolo is another illustration of just how good Napoli have been this season, with the crushing 4-0 win at AC Milan in early October a sign of what the Partenopei are truly capable of.

Juventus were always likely to be favourites for the Scudetto on Coral and any other football odds site as their dominance of Italian football threatens to extend into its fifth season, so it is perhaps refreshing from a purista s perspective that Napoli have emerged as real contenders to challenge the Bianconeri. It is the sort of purple patch that any striker worth their salt would dream to be in; Coral have unsurprisingly backed Higuain as favourite to score in their next game against Sarria s former employers Empoli who have kept just one clean sheet from their last five league fixtures. Napoli will need Higuain to carry his rich vein of form throughout the rest of the season if they are to have any chance of maintaining their wonderful pace and sprint clear of the chasing pack.

Napoli have won many admirers across Europe for the quality of football they have played this season, but it remains to be seen if they have the mentality to pass the acid test and keep the momentum going between now and the end of the season. Recent history would suggest that their chances are not great; the Partenopei, then managed by Walter Mazzarri, put themselves in a wonderful position in 2012/2013, only to finish runners-up behind Juventus as the odd slip at the wrong times proved costly in their pursuit of Juventus. A number of third-placed finishes would also suggest that Napoli have lacked the mentality and guile to end their long wait for a Scudetto, but there is real excitement in Naples that the current crop of players have what it takes to stop the Old Lady from making it five titles in a row.

#1793. Why Tottenham's 'rock' Jan Paul van Hecke is being compared to Bobby Moore and Stuart Pearce: 'Releasing the beast', a 'Zeeland Army' watching his every move and how high-risk passing is paying off

Published: 07:00 EST, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 07:14 EST, 5 November 2026

With his roots in a humble fishing community, World Cup pedigree in the family and glowing comparisons to a couple of England legends, it is perhaps no surprise to find Jan Paul van Hecke emerging as Tottenham's anchorman after a turbulent start to the season.

Van Hecke's strength of character shone through when things went badly awry and Spurs sank to the bottom of the Premier League, winless in the first five games, then rose from the depths with 10 points from the next four.

His ability and influence would never have been in doubt as far as Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi was concerned, having worked with Van Hecke for two years at Brighton. The 26-year-old Dutch centre-half leaves a positive impression wherever he plays.

'JP is a real force,' says Peter Maas, technical director of NAC Breda, where Van Hecke began his professional career. 'He is a rock. He will never back off. He will never let his team down. Never, never. He is truly one of a kind. A good lad with a good heart.

'I've always compared his presence and commitment to Stuart Pearce, "Psycho" back in the '80s and '90s. He was crazy, eh? Every now and then, JP will release the beast and let everything out.

'But he can play football, too. He can defend in an old-school way, but he can also build play in the modern way and is certainly more composed now.'

Jan Paul van Hecke has been Tottenham's anchorman this season, as they recovered from a woeful start to take 10 points from their last four league games

He tops Spurs' charts for clearances and duels won - as well as having completed more forward passes and more line-breaking passes than any other outfielder in the Premier League

Van Hecke's uncle Jan Poortvliet (centre, facing camera) was a defender in the Netherlands team which lost to Argentina in the 1978 World Cup final

Van Hecke's uncle Jan Poortvliet was a defender in the Netherlands team which made it to the World Cup final in 1978, and 30 years later had a brief spell as Southampton manager in the Championship. Jan Paul needs one more cap to match Poortvliet's tally of 19 for his country.

Blackburn boss Tony Mowbray, a fearless centre-half as a player, compared Van Hecke to another blond England legend after luring him to Ewood Park on loan from Brighton in 2021. The Seagulls had signed Van Hecke for £1.8million the year before and sold him to Spurs this summer for £54m.

'I've got to be careful I don't overbuild him as he's not our player,' said Mowbray at the time. 'But he looks like Bobby Moore out there sometimes. It's amazing to watch how composed, how calm he can be, yet he has the fire of a warrior in his belly.'

Van Hecke's vision and passing range combined with his natural aggression and appetite for sporting conflict appeals to the modern coach.

He meets the physical demands of the Premier League with relish, hailing from Arnemuiden, an isolated town of 5,000 in the province of Zeeland with a deep-rooted fishing history and a reputation for resilience through times of hardship.

It is now home to an army of devoted Van Hecke fans who cross the North Sea to watch him play at every opportunity. One hundred made the journey to see him score against Crystal Palace last Saturday.

Another element of Van Hecke's early impact in N17 has been his readiness to accept the ball, often in difficult areas, and search for forward passes through the lines.

It has led to mistakes which irritated some Spurs fans during their terrible start to the campaign, but De Zerbi demands this high-risk style and Van Hecke to his credit resisted the temptation to play with greater caution even though it would have spared him some of the criticism.

Van Hecke made such an impression on Tony Mowbray on loan at Blackburn in 2021-22 that he compared him to Bobby Moore

His impact is clear from his data. Van Hecke has played every minute of the Premier League campaign, starting the game at Manchester United last month despite returning from international duty with stitches in a wound on the top of his foot.

He has completed more forward passes (258) and more line-breaking passes (150) than any outfielder in the Premier League. Only Arsenal duo Martin Odegaard (197) and Declan Rice (177) have made more successful passes into the final third than his 174, only Manchester City's Ruben Dias (819) has played more passes than his 809, and Van Hecke leads the Spurs ranks for clearances and duels won. For good measure, he is also the club's top scorer – albeit with only two goals.

His desire to shoulder responsibility even in difficult times is exactly the type of leadership by example Spurs have lacked in recent years.

'He excelled in one-on-one defending but above all in his mentality,' Maas tells Daily Mail Sport as he reflects on Van Hecke's early development after joining NAC from amateur team VV Goes at the age of 18.

'What struck me was that when faced with setbacks, or a kick or a blow to the head on the pitch, he always got back up with even greater determination. It was as if the adrenaline helped him become unbeatable.

'That's where he channelled his energy. First at NAC in the second tier, then at Heerenveen in the Eredivisie. At Brighton, too. Step by step, he gets 10 per cent better every time because he adapts easily to his surroundings.'

There were times when the teenage Van Hecke might display frustration to be on the fringes of the team at NAC. Competition for places at the back included Colin Rosler, a graduate of the Manchester City academy where his father Uwe was a hero and who now plays in Denmark for AGF.

'Until the winter of 2019, JP was mainly a substitute and clearly struggling with that,' recalls Maas, who left the head scout's role at NAC for the same post at Heerenveen in 2021 before returning as NAC technical director two years later.

Van Hecke is Spurs' top scorer in the Premier League this season - albeit with only two goals

'It was impossible to predict he would make the upper echelons of the Premier League and the Dutch national team,' says Maas. 'But you could certainly see he had great potential'

'He felt it was unfair that he wasn't playing and went through a rough patch and was showing it. He actually lost the will to play, and I held a mirror to him once during a chat in the players' lounge and told him he had to prove himself.'

Helped by a change of head coach, Van Hecke broke into the first team and became integral to second-tier NAC's run to the semi-finals of the Dutch Cup, beating PSV Eindhoven and AZ Alkmaar before losing to Feyenoord.

His success came to personify the fighting spirit of NAC and he became the poster boy for their prolific youth development programme, with Bart Verbruggen, Van Hecke's team-mate at Brighton, also a graduate.

'It was impossible to predict he would make the upper echelons of the Premier League and the Dutch national team,' says Maas. 'But you could certainly see he had great potential and he will continue to improve because his immense drive will take him further.'
